docs.title: Soft Potato Development Roadmap
docs.text:
This document outlines the strategic development plan and versioning milestones for Soft Potato (3.x series).

Soft Potato adheres to Semantic Versioning (SemVer 2.0.0) and PEP 440: - Major release (3.0.0): Establishes the new stable architecture and API baseline following the complete version 3 rewrite. - Minor releases (3.x.0): Introduce new, backwards-compatible domain modules and functional enhancements without breaking existing APIs. - Patch releases (3.x.y): Bug fixes, performance optimizations, and documentation improvements.

docs.title: Milestone Overview
docs.text: Milestone Target Version Focus Area Status Release Type State Stabilization v3.0.0 Finalize core solver module & solve_ivp integration Released Stable Baseline Milestone 1: Analytical Equations v3.1.0 Analytical & empirical equations, simulation benchmarks & parameter fitting Released Minor Feature Addition Milestone 2: Grids v3.2.0 Spatial discretization & non-uniform/expanding meshes Released Minor Feature Addition Milestone 3: Reactions v3.3.0 Homogeneous & heterogeneous chemical reaction kinetics Released Minor Feature Addition Milestone 4: Techniques v3.4.0 Electrochemical waveform generators, simulation pipelines, plotting & diagnostics Released Minor Feature Addition Milestone 5: Documentation Overhaul v3.4.1 Clean-slate MkDocs restructure by expertise level (Experimentalist, Python User, Modeller) Released Documentation & Patch

docs.title: State Stabilization: v3.0.0
docs.text: Goal: Finalize the current solver module (including the solve_ivp integration) and release it as the new stable baseline for the Soft Potato 3.x series.

docs.title: Objectives & Deliverables
docs.text:
• Core Solver Module (softpotato.solver):
  • Consolidate and finalize the unified PDE problem formulation:
    • DiffusionProblem: 1D multi-species diffusion and reaction-diffusion specification with strict validation for positive diffusion coefficients (\(D_i > 0\)), initial conditions, and domain boundaries.
    • BoundaryCondition: Robust abstraction supporting Dirichlet (DirichletBC) and Neumann (NeumannBC) boundary conditions with constant values or time-dependent callables \(f(t)\).
    • SolverResult: Structured output container providing spatial and temporal concentration distributions, dict-like species access (result["A"]), and automated interfacial flux calculation (\(J_i = -D_i \left.\frac{\partial c_i}{\partial x}\right|_{x=0}\)).
  • scipy_ivp Solver Integration:
  • Finalize the Method of Lines (MOL) semi-discretization engine (ScipyIVPSolver) leveraging scipy.integrate.solve_ivp.
  • Default to high-order stiff ODE/DAE integrators (implicit 5th-order Runge-Kutta Radau and BDF), crucial for steep electrochemical concentration gradients and stiff boundary kinetics.
  • Support user-configurable integration tolerances (rtol, atol) and adaptive time-stepping.
  • Classical Finite Difference Solvers:
  • CrankNicolson: Second-order implicit scheme (\(\mathcal{O}(\Delta t^2, \Delta x^2)\)) using efficient tridiagonal banded solvers (scipy.linalg.solve_banded).
  • ImplicitFiniteDifference (BTCS): Unconditionally stable first-order implicit scheme (\(\mathcal{O}(\Delta t, \Delta x^2)\)) resistant to high-frequency initial-condition shocks.
  • ExplicitFiniteDifference (FTCS): Conditionally stable explicit scheme (\(\mathcal{O}(\Delta t, \Delta x^2)\)) with Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) stability verification (\(\Delta t \le \frac{\Delta x^2}{2 D_{\max}}\)) and automated substepping.
  • Verification & Quality Assurance:
  • Validate all solvers against exact analytical solutions (Fourier sine decay, Cottrell chronoamperometry, and total mass conservation under zero-flux boundaries).
  • Reach 100% passing unit and benchmark tests across Python 3.10–3.13.
  • Complete Sphinx documentation with Read the Docs integration and interactive Jupyter tutorials.
  • Release Status:
  • Successfully stabilized and released v3.0.0 as the official stable baseline.

docs.title: Milestone 1 (Analytical Equations): v3.1.0
docs.text: Goal: Introduce a dedicated, vectorized analytical and empirical electrochemistry equations module (softpotato.analytical), providing exact benchmark solutions for numerical solvers, parameter estimation and curve fitting utilities for experimental data, and rapid response comparison tools.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: Analytical and empirical equations form the classical bedrock of electrochemistry. While numerical PDE solvers are indispensable for complex geometries, coupled homogeneous reaction mechanisms, or arbitrary potential waveforms, closed-form analytical solutions provide: 1. Exact Ground-Truth Benchmarking: Rigorous validation standards to verify numerical solvers (softpotato.solver), ensuring spatial and temporal discretization convergence, flux conservation, and boundary stencil fidelity without truncation errors. 2. Instant Parameter Fitting & Estimation: Direct extraction of key physical and kinetic parameters (\(D\), \(k^0\), \(\alpha\), \(c^*\), electrode area \(A\), microdisc radius \(a\), spherical radius \(r\)) from experimental or simulated data via non-linear regression, eliminating the computational cost of iterative PDE solving in optimization loops. 3. Rapid Response Comparison & Screening: Instantaneous theoretical baselines for voltammetric, chronoamperometric, hydrodynamic, microelectrode, SECM, and steady-state responses to rapidly interpret experimental observations and inform numerical model configuration.

docs.title: Objectives & Deliverables
docs.text:
• Transient Diffusion & Potential Step Equations (softpotato.analytical.diffusion / softpotato.analytical.step):

  • cottrell: Planar Cottrell equation for semi-infinite linear diffusion chronoamperometry:

    \[ I(t) = \frac{n F A \sqrt{D} c^*}{\sqrt{\pi t}} \]

  • cottrell_spherical: Cottrell equation for spherical electrodes, hanging mercury drops, and micro-spheres of radius \(r\):

    \[ I(t) = n F A D c^* \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\pi D t}} + \frac{1}{r}\right) \]

  • cottrell_step: Double potential step chronoamperometry reversal transient (\(I(t)\) for \(t > \tau\)).

  • anson: Anson equation for chronocoulometry cumulative charge transients:

    \[ Q(t) = \frac{2 n F A \sqrt{D} c^* \sqrt{t}}{\sqrt{\pi}} + Q_{\text{dl}} + n F A \Gamma \]

  • sand: Sand equation for chronopotentiometry transition time \(\tau\) under constant current:

    \[ I \tau^{1/2} = \frac{n F A \sqrt{\pi D} c^*}{2} \]

  • cottrell_cylinder: Short- and long-time asymptotic expansions for cylindrical wire/fiber electrodes.

  • Hydrodynamics & Convection Equations (softpotato.analytical.hydrodynamics):

  • levich: Levich equation for convective mass-transport limiting current at a Rotating Disk Electrode (RDE):

    \[ I_L = 0.620\, n F A D^{2/3} \omega^{1/2} \nu^{-1/6} c^* \]

  • koutecky_levich: Koutecký–Levich equation for mixed kinetic and mass-transfer limitation:

    \[ \frac{1}{I} = \frac{1}{I_K} + \frac{1}{I_L} = \frac{1}{n F A k(E) c^*} + \frac{1}{0.620\, n F A D^{2/3} \omega^{1/2} \nu^{-1/6} c^*} \]

  • rotating_ring_disk: Theoretical collection efficiency (\(N\)) and ring limiting currents for RRDE systems.

  • Microelectrode & Ultramicroelectrode (UME) Geometries (softpotato.analytical.microelectrodes):

  • microdisc_limiting_current: Saito steady-state limiting current for an inlaid microdisc of radius \(a\):

    \[ I_{\text{lim}} = 4 n F D c^* a \]

  • microdisc_transient: Shoup and Szabo empirical approximation for inlaid microdisc chronoamperometry with radius \(a\), spanning the entire transition from short-time planar Cottrell decay to long-time steady state (\(<0.6\%\) maximum relative error):

    \[ I(t) = \frac{4 n F D c^* a}{f(\tau)}, \quad \tau = \frac{4 D t}{a^2} \]

  • mahon_oldham_transient: Mahon and Oldham analytical expression for transient diffusion current at an inlaid microdisc electrode of radius \(a\) across all time regimes:

    \[ I(t) = 4 n F D c^* a \cdot f(\theta), \quad \theta = \frac{4 D t}{a^2} \]

  • microhemisphere_limiting_current & microsphere_limiting_current: Steady-state limiting currents for hemispherical (\(I_{\text{lim}} = 2 \pi n F D c^* r\)) and spherical (\(I_{\text{lim}} = 4 \pi n F D c^* r\)) microelectrodes of radius \(r\).

  • microband_limiting_current: Steady-state and quasi-steady-state current approximations for microband geometries.
  • Scanning Electrochemical Microscopy (SECM) Approach Curves (softpotato.analytical.secm):

  • secm_approach_positive_feedback: Lefrou and Cornut analytical approximation for steady-state normalized tip current (\(I_T = i_T / i_{T,\infty}\) with \(i_{T,\infty} = 4 n F D c^* a\)) over a conductive substrate (positive feedback / diffusion-controlled mediator regeneration) as a function of normalized distance (\(L = d / a\)) and insulator radius ratio (\(RG = r_g / a\)):

    \[ I_T^{\text{cond}}(L, RG) \]

  • secm_approach_negative_feedback: Lefrou and Cornut analytical approximation for steady-state normalized tip current over an insulating substrate (negative feedback / hindered diffusion) as a function of normalized distance (\(L = d / a\)) and insulator radius ratio (\(RG = r_g / a\)):

    \[ I_T^{\text{ins}}(L, RG) \]

  • Voltammetry & Kinetic Diagnostics (softpotato.analytical.voltammetry):

  • randles_sevcik: Randles–Ševčík peak current for reversible electron transfer at planar electrodes:

    \[ I_p = 0.4463\, n F A c^* \sqrt{\frac{n F D v}{R T}} \]

  • randles_sevcik_irreversible: Peak current for totally irreversible electron transfer:

    \[ I_p = 0.4958\, n F A c^* \sqrt{\frac{\alpha n_\alpha F D v}{R T}} \]

  • randles_sevcik_quasi: Peak current and shape factor approximations across intermediate quasi-reversible regimes.

  • peak_potential_irreversible: Peak potential shift relationship with scan rate \(v\) for irreversible systems.
  • nicholson_psi: Nicholson method relating peak potential separation (\(\Delta E_p\)) to the dimensionless kinetic parameter \(\Psi\) and standard rate constant \(k^0\), providing both forward rational approximations and inverse solvers.
  • matsuda_ayabe: Dimensionless parameter \(\Lambda\) boundary criteria classifying reversible (\(\Lambda \ge 15\)), quasi-reversible (\(10^{-3} < \Lambda < 15\)), and irreversible (\(\Lambda \le 10^{-3}\)) voltammetric systems.
  • Thermodynamics & Interfacial Kinetics (softpotato.analytical.kinetics):

  • nernst: Nernst equation for equilibrium electrode potential and surface concentration ratios:

    \[ E = E^{0\prime} + \frac{R T}{n F} \ln\left(\frac{c_{\text{Ox}}}{c_{\text{Red}}}\right) \]

  • butler_volmer: Butler–Volmer equation for current density and net current as a function of overpotential \(\eta = E - E^{0\prime}\):

    \[ I = I_0 \left[\exp\left(\frac{(1 - \alpha) n F \eta}{R T}\right) - \exp\left(-\frac{\alpha n F \eta}{R T}\right)\right], \quad I_0 = n F A k^0 (c_{\text{Ox}}^*)^{1-\alpha} (c_{\text{Red}}^*)^\alpha \]

  • tafel: Anodic and cathodic high-overpotential Tafel approximations (\(\eta = a + b \log_{10}|I|\)) with automated extraction of Tafel slopes (\(b\)) and exchange currents (\(I_0\)).

  • Simulation Benchmarking Suite (softpotato.analytical.benchmark):
  • Automated benchmark harness comparing softpotato.solver numerical results against analytical solutions.
  • Standardized error metrics: Root-Mean-Square Error (RMSE), maximum pointwise deviation (\(L_\infty\)), relative error, and order-of-convergence verification across \(\Delta x\) and \(\Delta t\).
  • Parameter Fitting & Experimental Data Analysis (softpotato.analytical.fitting):
  • Optimization wrappers around scipy.optimize.curve_fit / least_squares with physically bounded parameter constraints (\(D > 0\), \(0 < \alpha < 1\), \(k^0 \ge 0\), \(c^* \ge 0\), \(A > 0\), \(a > 0\), \(r > 0\)).
  • Direct linear and non-linear regression utilities: Cottrell \(I\) vs. \(t^{-1/2}\), Randles–Ševčík \(I_p\) vs. \(v^{1/2}\), Levich \(I_L\) vs. \(\omega^{1/2}\), Koutecký–Levich \(1/I\) vs. \(\omega^{-1/2}\), Tafel plots (\(\eta\) vs. \(\log_{10}|I|\)), and SECM approach curve fitting (\(RG\), distance \(d\), and tip offset).
  • Statistical confidence intervals, standard errors, parameter correlation matrices, and goodness-of-fit indicators (\(R^2\), reduced \(\chi^2\)).
  • Architecture & Compatibility:
  • Fully vectorized NumPy implementations supporting scalar and array inputs with dimensional broadcasting.
  • Centralized physical constants (FARADAY, GAS_CONSTANT, STANDARD_TEMPERATURE) with explicit unit conventions.
  • Release Status:
  • Successfully implemented, benchmarked, tested, and released as v3.1.0.

docs.title: Milestone 2 (Grids): v3.2.0
docs.text:
Status: Released

Goal: Introduce a dedicated spatial discretization and meshing module (softpotato.grid), adding non-uniform and expanding grids as a new, backwards-compatible feature.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: In electrochemical simulations, diffusion layers are typically confined to a narrow region adjacent to the electrode surface (\(x=0\)). Uniform grids require an excessively large number of spatial points (\(N_x\)) to resolve steep surface gradients, inflating computational cost. Expanding grids concentrate spatial resolution near the electrode while coarsening into the bulk solution, delivering orders-of-magnitude faster simulations without sacrificing precision.

docs.title: Objectives & Deliverables
docs.text:
• Meshing Module (softpotato.grid):
  • Uniform1DMesh: Standard equidistant grid generator.

  • GeometricExpandingMesh: Exponential / geometrically expanding spatial discretization:

    \[ \Delta x_j = \Delta x_0 \cdot \gamma^j \quad (\gamma > 1) \]

  • ExponentialMesh and conformal transformation-based coordinates for semi-infinite diffusion domains.

  • Non-Uniform Discretization Operators:
  • Implement second-order finite difference stencils adapted for non-uniform spacing for both first (\(\partial c / \partial x\)) and second (\(\partial^2 c / \partial x^2\)) spatial derivatives.
  • Ghost-node and boundary stencil formulations on irregular node intervals for Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions.
  • Backwards Compatibility:
  • Ensure DiffusionProblem seamlessly accepts either raw 1D NumPy arrays (np.ndarray) or structured mesh objects (Mesh1D).
  • Existing v3.0.0, v3.1.0, and v3.1.1 solver scripts and tutorials continue executing with zero code changes.
  • Solver Adaptations:
  • Enable ScipyIVPSolver and banded implicit solvers to consume non-uniform spatial discretizations natively.
  • Release Status:
  • Successfully implemented, benchmarked, tested, and released as v3.2.0.

docs.title: Milestone 3 (Reactions): v3.3.0
docs.text:
Status: Released

Goal: Introduce a comprehensive chemical and electrochemical kinetics module (softpotato.reactions), providing modular multi-species reaction mechanisms.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: Electrochemical systems frequently involve coupled chemical transformations (e.g., EC, EC', ECE, catalytic, and disproportionation pathways) as well as non-linear interfacial charge-transfer kinetics. A dedicated reactions module decouples kinetic mechanism definitions from the spatial diffusion solvers.

docs.title: Objectives & Deliverables
docs.text:
• Chemical Species Abstraction (softpotato.reactions.species):
  • Species: Immutable dataclass encapsulating species identity, standard diffusion coefficient (\(D_i\)), bulk concentration (\(c_i^*\)), formal charge (\(z_i\)), standard redox potential (\(E^{0\prime}\)), and electron transfer count (\(n\)).
  • SpeciesCollection: Ordered mapping container providing dict-like lookup and direct export helpers (diffusivities, bulk_concentrations, n_electrons_map) for DiffusionProblem.
  • Homogeneous Reaction Kinetics (softpotato.reactions.homogeneous):

  • Flexible multi-reaction formulation (ReactionNetwork) computing reaction rate vectors \(\mathbf{R}(\mathbf{c}, x, t)\):

    \[ \frac{\partial c_i}{\partial t} = D_i \nabla^2 c_i + R_i(\mathbf{c}) \]

  • Built-in reaction primitives: FirstOrderReaction, ReversibleReaction (\(A \rightleftharpoons B\)), SecondOrderReaction, DimerizationReaction, DisproportionationReaction, CatalyticReaction (EC'), general MassActionReaction, and extensible CustomReaction.

  • Automated analytical sparse kinetic Jacobian assembly for implicit stiff ODE integration (Radau, BDF).
  • Heterogeneous Charge-Transfer Kinetics (softpotato.reactions.heterogeneous):

  • Butler–Volmer kinetics (ButlerVolmer):

    \[ k_f = k^0 \exp\left(-\frac{\alpha n F}{R T}(E(t) - E^{0\prime})\right), \quad k_b = k^0 \exp\left(\frac{(1 - \alpha) n F}{R T}(E(t) - E^{0\prime})\right) \]

  • High-overpotential unidirectional Tafel kinetics (TafelKinetics / Tafel).

  • Reversible Nernstian equilibrium (NernstianEquilibrium) and boundary condition factory (create_electrochemical_bcs).
  • Mechanism Abstractions & Solver Integration (softpotato.reactions.mechanisms, softpotato.solver):
  • ElectrochemicalStep, Mechanism, and CustomMechanism packaging species, homogeneous steps, and interfacial kinetics independently of grid and solver.
  • Plug-and-play linkage with DiffusionProblem(..., species=..., reactions=..., mechanism=...) and sparse kinetic Jacobian integration in ScipyIVPSolver.
  • Backwards-compatible: DiffusionProblem remains fully functional without explicit reaction definitions.
  • Validation & Documentation:
  • Analytical benchmark suite (tests/test_reactions_benchmark.py) verifying EC' catalytic limiting currents, Delahay–Stiehl transients, equilibrium relaxation, mass conservation, and Butler–Volmer CV diagnostics against Randles–Ševčík and Nicholson theory.
  • Complete MkDocs API reference (docs/api/reactions.md) and interactive tutorials (examples/catalytic_ec.ipynb, examples/heterogeneous_kinetics.ipynb).
  • Release Status:
  • Successfully implemented, benchmarked, tested, and released as v3.3.0.

docs.title: Milestone 4 (Techniques): v3.4.0
docs.text:
Status: Released

Goal: Introduce high-level electrochemical experimental techniques and waveform generators (softpotato.techniques), enabling turnkey simulation, declarative plotting, and diagnostic workflows.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: With solvers, analytical benchmark models, grids, and reaction kinetics in place, users need standard experimental protocols (voltammetry, chronoamperometry, pulse techniques, chronopotentiometry, RDE) and automated signal, plotting, and diagnostic pipelines without manually coding potential excitation waveforms and boundary conditions.

docs.title: Objectives & Deliverables
docs.text:
• Waveform & Signal Generators (softpotato.techniques):
  • Chronoamperometry: Single-, double-, and multi-potential step sequences with configurable pulse durations and resting times.
  • LinearSweepVoltammetry (LSV): Unidirectional potential sweeps with configurable start/end potentials and scan rates (\(v\)).
  • CyclicVoltammetry (CV): Multi-cycle triangular potential waveforms with customizable vertices and switching potentials.
  • RotatingDiskElectrode (RDE), RDESweep, simulate_rde_sweep: Hydrodynamic convective-diffusion modeling under the Levich (levich_convection) and Nernst stagnant diffusion layer (nernst_layer) approximations.
  • PulseTechniques & Chronopotentiometry: SampledCurrentVoltammetry (SCV), DifferentialPulseVoltammetry (DPV), SquareWaveVoltammetry (SWV), and galvanostatic Chronopotentiometry (CP).
  • CustomWaveform: Composite excitation generator allowing arbitrary chaining of ConstantSegment, LinearRampSegment, SinusoidalSegment, and CallableSegment segments.
  • Simulation Pipeline Orchestrator:
  • High-level execution API (simulate, simulate_sweep) returning TechniqueResult and coordinating physics-informed grid creation, boundary condition assignment, event-aware piecewise integration, and Faradaic current/charge extraction.
  • Declarative Plotting Interfaces (softpotato.techniques.plotting):
  • Technique-aware PlotSpec, PLOT_ALIASES, resolve_plot_kind, plot_result (result.plot()), plot_summary (result.plot_summary()), and plot_sweep.
  • Dedicated renderers (plot_voltammogram, plot_current_vs_time, plot_potential_vs_time, plot_concentration_profile, plot_charge_vs_time, plot_scv, plot_dpv, plot_swv) and diagnostic plots (plot_peaks, plot_randles_sevcik, plot_cottrell, plot_levich, plot_koutecky_levich, plot_tafel).
  • Post-Processing & Electrochemical Diagnostics:
  • Automated peak detection (find_peaks returning CVDiagnostics / PeakInfo).
  • Diagnostics: analyze_randles_sevcik, analyze_nicholson, analyze_levich, analyze_koutecky_levich, analyze_tafel, analyze_cottrell, and analyze_sand leveraging softpotato.analytical.
  • Backwards Compatibility:
  • Modular addition that imports and utilizes softpotato.solver, softpotato.analytical, softpotato.grid, and softpotato.reactions without breaking lower-level solver APIs.

docs.title: Milestone 5 (Documentation Overhaul): v3.4.1
docs.text:
Status: Released (GitHub Milestone #6, Issues #104–#112)

Goal: Rebuild softpotato.xyz from a clean slate so users of any background—experimental electrochemists with no programming experience, Python users new to modelling, and computational modellers—can immediately locate what they need.

docs.title: Objectives & Deliverables
docs.text:
• Clean-Slate MkDocs Restructure (#104, #105):
  • Remove legacy, fragmented documentation and reorganize mkdocs.yml around user-intent tabs (Start Here, User Guide, Concepts, Tutorials, API Reference, Blog & Releases).
  • Add a 3-persona router on the home page and a decision table in Start Here.
  • Level 1 — Experimentalist (#106):
  • Zero-install Google Colab quickstart, local Python setup, "Run All" starter notebooks, and 5-minute copy-paste .py recipes (analytical, fitting, techniques.simulate()).
  • Level 2 — Python User (#107, #108, #109):
  • Task-oriented User Guide covering all softpotato.techniques, diagnostics, plotting, and analytical/fitting workflows with standalone .py scripts.
  • Pure-Markdown Concepts section bridging electrochemical theory (kinetics, transport, mechanisms) and numerical modelling (grids, solvers, benchmarking).
  • Level 3 — Modeller & Interactive Notebooks (#110, #111):
  • Curated Jupyter notebooks grouped by technique (CA, CV, Pulse, RDE), mechanism/geometry (Nernst, Randles–Ševčík, Butler–Volmer, EC, EE, Catalytic), and low-level module (analytical, fitting, solver, geometry, grid, reactions).
  • API Reference & Strict Validation (#112):
  • Complete mkdocstrings API reference for all softpotato modules and mkdocs build --strict CI verification.

docs.title: Summary of Semantic Versioning Strategy
docs.text:
v3.0.0 (Stable Baseline)
 └── Core Solvers Finalized (scipy_ivp, Crank-Nicolson, Implicit, Explicit)
      │
      ├── v3.1.0 (Minor Bump: Non-breaking feature)
      │    └── Analytical & empirical electrochemical equations (softpotato.analytical)
      │
      ├── v3.2.0 (Minor Bump: Non-breaking feature)
      │    └── Non-uniform and expanding spatial grids (softpotato.grid)
      │
      ├── v3.3.0 (Minor Bump: Non-breaking feature)
      │    └── Homogeneous & heterogeneous chemical reactions (softpotato.reactions)
      │
      └── v3.4.0 (Minor Bump: Non-breaking feature)
           ├── Electroanalytical techniques & waveforms (softpotato.techniques)
           └── v3.4.1 (Patch: Documentation overhaul — Milestone 5)

Each minor release maintains strict backwards compatibility with previous releases, ensuring scripts written against v3.0.0 continue to run unmodified throughout the entire 3.x lifecycle.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Welcome to the Soft Potato API Reference. The toolkit is organized into modular subpackages and modules for physical constants, closed-form analytical electrochemistry, coordinate geometries, non-uniform spatial discretization meshes, chemical and electrochemical reaction kinetics, and numerical PDE solvers.

docs.title: Constants Module
docs.text:
The softpotato.constants module provides standardized physical and electrochemical constants defined according to CODATA 2018 / 2019 SI conventions [1].

Constant / Identifier Symbol Value & Units FARADAY (F) \(F\) \(96485.332 \,\text{C}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\) GAS_CONSTANT (R) \(R\) \(8.31446\,\text{J}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\cdot\text{K}^{-1}\) STANDARD_TEMPERATURE (T_STD) \(T^\circ\) \(298.15\,\text{K}\) (\(25\,^\circ\text{C}\)) AVOGADRO \(N_{\text{A}}\) \(6.02214 \times 10^{23}\,\text{mol}^{-1}\) BOLTZMANN \(k_{\text{B}}\) \(1.38065 \times 10^{-23}\,\text{J}\cdot\text{K}^{-1}\) ELEMENTARY_CHARGE \(e\) \(1.60218 \times 10^{-19}\,\text{C}\) VACUUM_PERMITTIVITY \(\varepsilon_0\) \(8.85419 \times 10^{-12}\,\text{F}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}\)

docs.title: Analytical Module
docs.text: The softpotato.analytical subpackage provides closed-form analytical solutions, asymptotic approximations, and diagnostic formulations across transient step techniques, hydrodynamics, interfacial kinetics, voltammetry, microelectrodes, SECM, parameter fitting, and numerical benchmark suites.

docs.title: Transient Step Techniques
docs.text:
The softpotato.analytical.step module provides exact solutions for potentiostatic and galvanostatic step experiments, including Cottrell, Anson, and Sand formulations.

Function Inputs Output Description References cottrell \(t, n, D, c^*, A\) \(I(t)\) Planar chronoamperometric diffusion-limited current transient. 2 cottrell_step \(t, \tau, n, D, c^*, A, D_{\text{Red}}\) \(I(t)\) Double potential step chronoamperometry reversal current. 3 cottrell_spherical \(t, r, n, D, c^*, A\) \(I(t)\) Chronoamperometric current at a spherical electrode. 3 cottrell_cylinder \(t, r_0, n, D, c^*, l, A\) \(I(t)\) Chronoamperometric current at a cylindrical wire/fiber electrode. 4, 5 anson \(t, n, D, c^*, A, Q_{\text{dl}}, \Gamma, \tau\) \(Q(t)\) Cumulative charge transient for chronocoulometry. 6 sand \(t, I, n, D, c^*, A\) \(c(0, t)\) Surface reactant concentration transient under constant current. 7 sand_transition_time \(I, n, D, c^*, A\) \(\tau\) Transition time for galvanostatic chronopotentiometry. 7 sand_potential \(t, \tau, E_{1/2}, n, T\) \(E(t)\) Potential-time response curve for chronopotentiometry. 7 step_concentration_profile \(x, t, D, c^*\) \(c(x, t)\) Exact spatial concentration profile following a potential step. 8 step_flux_profile \(x, t, D, c^*\) \(J(x, t)\) Exact spatial diffusion flux profile following a potential step. 8

docs.title: Hydrodynamics & Convection Equations
docs.text:
The softpotato.analytical.hydrodynamics module provides models for rotating disk (RDE) and rotating ring-disk (RRDE) convective electrochemical systems.

Function Inputs Output Description References levich \(\omega, n, D, c^*, A, u\) \(I_{ ext{L}}\) Convective mass-transfer limiting current at an RDE. 9 levich_constant \(n, D, c^*, A, u\) \(B\) Theoretical Levich slope parameter for RDE rotation series. 9 koutecky_levich \(\omega, I_{ ext{k}}, k, I_{ ext{lim}}, n, D, c^*, A, u\) \(I\) Current under mixed kinetic and convective mass-transfer control. 10 koutecky_levich_analysis \(\omega, I, A, c^*, n, u\) \(k, B\) Kinetic rate constant and Levich slope extraction from RDE data. 10 nernst_diffusion_layer \(\omega, D, u\) \(\delta\) Steady-state stagnant diffusion layer thickness at an RDE. 9 collection_efficiency \(r_1, r_2, r_3\) \(N\) Theoretical collection efficiency for an RRDE geometry. 11 shielding_factor \(r_1, r_2, r_3, N\) \(S\) Theoretical geometric shielding factor for an RRDE. 11 ring_collection_current \(I_{ ext{disk}}, N, n_{ ext{ring}}, n_{ ext{disk}}\) \(I_{ ext{ring}}\) Ring electrode current from disk product collection. 11 ring_limiting_current \(\omega, r_1, r_2, r_3, n, D, c^*, u\) \(I_{ ext{R,lim}}\) Convective mass-transfer limiting current at an RRDE ring. 11 rotating_ring_disk \(r_1, r_2, r_3, \omega, n, D, c^*, u\) \(N, S, I_{ ext{D,lim}}, I_{ ext{R,lim}}\) Comprehensive collection and limiting current metrics for RRDE. 11 rad_s_to_rpm \(\omega\) \(f_{ ext{RPM}}\) Angular velocity to rotational speed conversion. rpm_to_rad_s \(f_{ ext{RPM}}\) \(\omega\) Rotational speed to angular velocity conversion.

docs.title: Thermodynamics & Interfacial Kinetics
docs.text:
The softpotato.analytical.kinetics module provides thermodynamic equilibrium potentials and electrode kinetic models, including Nernst, Butler–Volmer, and Tafel formulations.

Function Inputs Output Description References nernst \(E^\circ, c_{\text{Ox}}, c_{\text{Red}}, n, T\) \(E\) Reversible equilibrium reduction potential. 12 nernst_potential \(E^\circ, c_{\text{Ox}}, c_{\text{Red}}, n, T\) \(E\) Nernst equilibrium electrode potential calculation. 12 nernst_ratio \(E, E^\circ, n, T\) \(c_{\text{Ox}} / c_{\text{Red}}\) Equilibrium concentration ratio from applied potential. 12 nernst_equilibrium_concentrations \(E, E^\circ, c_{\text{total}}, n, T\) \(c_{\text{Ox}}, c_{\text{Red}}\) Individual equilibrium species concentrations from total pool. 12 butler_volmer \(\eta, I_0, \alpha, n, T\) \(I\) Faradaic current from activation overpotential. 13, 14 butler_volmer_current_density \(\eta, j_0, \alpha, n, T\) \(j\) Faradaic current density from activation overpotential. 13, 14 butler_volmer_linear \(\eta, I_0, n, T\) \(I\) Low-overpotential linearized Butler–Volmer current. 13, 14 charge_transfer_resistance \(I_0, n, T\) \(R_{\text{ct}}\) Charge-transfer resistance at equilibrium potential. 13, 14 exchange_current \(k_0, c_{\text{Ox}}^*, c_{\text{Red}}^*, A, \alpha, n\) \(I_0\) Standard exchange current from rate constant and concentrations. 13, 14 exchange_current_density \(k_0, c_{\text{Ox}}^*, c_{\text{Red}}^*, \alpha, n\) \(j_0\) Exchange current density from rate constant and concentrations. 13, 14 tafel \(\eta, I_0, \alpha, n, T\) \(I\) High-overpotential unidirectional Tafel current approximation. 15 tafel_overpotential \(I, I_0, \alpha, n, T\) \(\eta\) Activation overpotential calculated from current. 15 tafel_slope \(\alpha, n, T\) \(b\) Theoretical Tafel slope in Volts per decade. 15 tafel_analysis \(\eta, I, A, c^*, n, T\) \(I_0, \alpha, b\) Semi-logarithmic Tafel regression for kinetic parameter extraction. 15

docs.title: Voltammetry & Kinetic Diagnostics
docs.text:
The softpotato.analytical.voltammetry module provides peak current expressions and reversibility diagnostics for cyclic and linear sweep voltammetry.

Function Inputs Output Description References randles_sevcik \(v, c^*, D, A, n, T\) \(I_{\text{p}}\) Reversible electron transfer peak voltammetric current. 16, 17 randles_sevcik_irreversible \(v, \alpha, n_\alpha, c^*, D, A, n, T\) \(I_{\text{p}}\) Totally irreversible electron transfer peak current. 18, 19 randles_sevcik_quasi \(v, k_0, \Lambda, c^*, D, A, \alpha, n, T\) \(I_{\text{p}}\) Quasi-reversible voltammetric peak current and wave shape. 19 peak_potential_irreversible \(v, k_0, E^{\circ\prime}, D, \alpha, n_\alpha, T\) \(E_{\text{p}}\) Peak potential shift for totally irreversible kinetics. 18, 19 nicholson_delta_ep \(\psi, n\) \(\Delta E_{\text{p}}\) Peak potential separation from Nicholson parameter. 20, 21 nicholson_psi \(\Delta E_{\text{p}}, k_0, v, D, n, T\) \(\psi\) Nicholson dimensionless kinetic parameter calculation. 20, 21 nicholson_rate_constant \(\Delta E_{\text{p}}, v, D, n, T\) \(k_0\) Standard heterogeneous rate constant extraction from peak split. 20, 21 matsuda_ayabe_lambda \(k_0, v, D, n, T\) \(\Lambda\) Dimensionless Matsuda–Ayabe reversibility parameter. 19 matsuda_ayabe \(k_0, v, D, n, \alpha, T\) \(\Lambda, \text{zone}\) Reversibility classification (reversible, quasi, irreversible). 19

docs.title: Microelectrode Geometries
docs.text:
The softpotato.analytical.microelectrodes module provides steady-state and transient diffusion-limited current expressions for ultramicroelectrode (UME) geometries.

Function Inputs Output Description References microdisc_limiting_current \(a, n, D, c^*\) \(I_{\text{ss}}\) Saito steady-state limiting current at an inlaid circular microdisc. 22, 23 microdisc_transient \(t, a, n, D, c^*\) \(I(t)\) Shoup–Szabo full-time chronoamperometric transient at a microdisc. 24 mahon_oldham_transient \(t, a, n, D, c^*\) \(I(t)\) High-precision Mahon–Oldham chronoamperometric transient. 25 microsphere_limiting_current \(r, n, D, c^*\) \(I_{\text{ss}}\) Steady-state spherical diffusion-limited current. 22 microhemisphere_limiting_current \(r, n, D, c^*\) \(I_{\text{ss}}\) Steady-state hemispherical diffusion-limited current. 22 microband_limiting_current \(t, w, l, n, D, c^*\) \(I(t)\) Quasi-steady-state diffusion-limited current at an inlaid microband. 26, 27

docs.title: Scanning Electrochemical Microscopy
docs.text:
The softpotato.analytical.secm module provides normalized approach curve models and feedback current expressions for scanning electrochemical microscopy.

Function Inputs Output Description References secm_limiting_current_infinite \(a, n, D, c^*\) \(I_{\text{T},\infty}\) Unhindered bulk steady-state current at microelectrode tip. 22 secm_approach_curve \(L, R_{\text{g}}, \kappa\) \(I_{\text{T}}^{\text{norm}}\) Normalized tip approach curve over substrates of arbitrary kinetics. 28, 29 secm_approach_positive_feedback \(L, R_{\text{g}}\) \(I_{\text{T}}^{\text{norm}}\) Pure positive feedback approach curve over conductive substrate. 28, 29 secm_approach_negative_feedback \(L, R_{\text{g}}\) \(I_{\text{T}}^{\text{norm}}\) Pure negative feedback approach curve over insulating substrate. 28, 29 secm_tip_current \(L, R_{\text{g}}, \kappa, a, n, D, c^*\) \(I_{\text{T}}\) Dimensional steady-state tip current in Amperes. 28, 29

docs.title: Parameter Fitting & Regression
docs.text:

docs.title: Constants Module (softpotato.constants)
docs.text: The softpotato.constants module provides standardized physical and electrochemical constants defined according to CODATA 2018 / 2019 SI conventions.

docs.title: constants
docs.text:
Physical and chemical constants with standardized SI definitions.

This module provides fundamental physical and electrochemical constants sourced from CODATA (via scipy.constants) and standardized IUPAC conventions.

Constants Constant Symbol Value Units Description FARADAY \(F\) \(\approx 96485.332\) \(\text{C}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\) Faraday constant (\(F = e \cdot N_A\)); electric charge per mole of electrons GAS_CONSTANT \(R\) \(\approx 8.31446\) \(\text{J}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}\cdot\text{K}^{-1}\) Molar gas constant (\(R = k_B \cdot N_A\)); ideal gas law proportionality constant STANDARD_TEMPERATURE \(T^\circ\) \(298.15\) \(\text{K}\) Standard thermodynamic temperature (corresponding to \(25\,^\circ\text{C}\)) Aliases Alias Target Description F FARADAY Shorthand alias for Faraday constant (\(F\)) R GAS_CONSTANT Shorthand alias for molar gas constant (\(R\)) T_STD STANDARD_TEMPERATURE Shorthand alias for standard thermodynamic temperature (\(T^\circ\)) Related Physical Constants Constant Symbol Value Units Description AVOGADRO \(N_A\) \(6.02214076 \times 10^{23}\) \(\text{mol}^{-1}\) Avogadro constant; constituent particles per mole BOLTZMANN \(k_B\) \(1.380649 \times 10^{-23}\) \(\text{J}\cdot\text{K}^{-1}\) Boltzmann constant; relates kinetic energy to temperature ELEMENTARY_CHARGE \(e\) \(1.602176634 \times 10^{-19}\) \(\text{C}\) Elementary charge; electric charge of a single proton VACUUM_PERMITTIVITY \(\varepsilon_0\) \(\approx 8.854188 \times 10^{-12}\) \(\text{F}\cdot\text{m}^{-1}\) Vacuum permittivity; capability to permit electric fields

Examples:

>>> from softpotato.constants import FARADAY, GAS_CONSTANT, STANDARD_TEMPERATURE
>>> round(FARADAY, 2)
96485.33
>>> round(GAS_CONSTANT, 4)
8.3145
>>> STANDARD_TEMPERATURE
298.15
>>> from softpotato.constants import F, R, T_STD
>>> F == FARADAY and R == GAS_CONSTANT and T_STD == STANDARD_TEMPERATURE
True

docs.title: Coordinate Geometries and Differential Operators
docs.text: Geometry Class & Aliases Symmetry Factor (\(p\)) Laplacian Operator (\(\nabla^2 c\)) Active Surface Area (\(A\)) PlanarGeometry ('planar', 'cartesian', '1d', 'linear') \(p = 0\) \(\dfrac{\partial^2 c}{\partial x^2}\) User-specified \(A\) (default \(1.0\)) CylindricalGeometry ('cylindrical', 'cylinder', 'wire') \(p = 1\) \(\dfrac{\partial^2 c}{\partial r^2} + \dfrac{1}{r}\dfrac{\partial c}{\partial r}\) \(2 \pi r_0 L\) SphericalGeometry ('spherical', 'sphere', 'hemispherical', 'hemisphere') \(p = 2\) \(\dfrac{\partial^2 c}{\partial r^2} + \dfrac{2}{r}\dfrac{\partial c}{\partial r}\) \(4 \pi r_0^2\) (full sphere) or \(2 \pi r_0^2\) (hemisphere)

docs.title: geometry
docs.text:
Spatial coordinate geometries and differential operators for electrochemical simulation.

This subpackage abstracts coordinate system metrics, spatial finite-difference operators (\(\nabla^2\), \(\nabla\)), normal interfacial flux evaluation, and active electrode surface integration:

\[ \nabla^2 c = \frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial r^2} + \frac{p}{r} \frac{\partial c}{\partial r} \]

Available built-in geometries include:

  • PlanarGeometry ("planar", \(p = 0\)): 1D Cartesian linear diffusion perpendicular to a planar macroelectrode.
  • SphericalGeometry ("spherical", "hemispherical", \(p = 2\)): 1D radial diffusion to a full spherical or hemispherical electrode.
  • CylindricalGeometry ("cylindrical", \(p = 1\)): 1D axisymmetric radial diffusion to a cylindrical wire or fiber microelectrode.

Examples:

Evaluating spatial operators across planar, spherical, and cylindrical geometries:

>>> import numpy as np
>>> from softpotato.geometry import (
...     PlanarGeometry,
...     SphericalGeometry,
...     CylindricalGeometry,
...     get_geometry,
... )
>>>
>>> planar = get_geometry("planar", area=1.0)
>>> x = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 51)
>>> bool(np.allclose(planar.laplacian(x**2, x), 2.0))
True
>>>
>>> sphere = SphericalGeometry(r0=1e-4)
>>> r = np.linspace(1.0, 5.0, 201)
>>> bool(np.max(np.abs(sphere.laplacian(1.0 / r, r)[1:-1])) < 1e-4)
True
>>>
>>> cylinder = CylindricalGeometry(r0=5e-6, length=1e-2)
>>> bool(np.max(np.abs(cylinder.laplacian(np.log(r), r)[1:-1])) < 1e-4)
True

docs.title: Geometry
docs.text:
Bases: ABC

Abstract base class representing spatial domain coordinate geometry.

Encapsulates coordinate metrics, finite-difference differential operators (\(\nabla^2\), \(\nabla\)), normal interfacial flux evaluation, and active electrode surface area integration for 1D and curvilinear coordinate systems:

\[ \nabla^2 c = \frac{1}{r^p} \frac{\partial}{\partial r} \left( r^p \frac{\partial c}{\partial r} \right) = \frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial r^2} + \frac{p}{r} \frac{\partial c}{\partial r} \]

where \(p = 0\) corresponds to planar Cartesian coordinates (\(x\)), \(p = 1\) to cylindrical radial coordinates (\(r\)), and \(p = 2\) to spherical radial coordinates (\(r\)).

class Geometry(ABC, metaclass=_GeometryMeta):
    r"""Abstract base class representing spatial domain coordinate geometry.

    Encapsulates coordinate metrics, finite-difference differential operators
    (:math:`\nabla^2`, :math:`\nabla`), normal interfacial flux evaluation, and
    active electrode surface area integration for 1D and curvilinear coordinate
    systems:

    .. math::

        \nabla^2 c = \frac{1}{r^p} \frac{\partial}{\partial r}
                     \left( r^p \frac{\partial c}{\partial r} \right)
                   = \frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial r^2} + \frac{p}{r} \frac{\partial c}{\partial r}

    where :math:`p = 0` corresponds to planar Cartesian coordinates (:math:`x`),
    :math:`p = 1` to cylindrical radial coordinates (:math:`r`), and :math:`p = 2`
    to spherical radial coordinates (:math:`r`).

    Attributes
    ----------
    name : str
        Canonical identifier of the coordinate geometry (e.g., ``'planar'``,
        ``'spherical'``, ``'cylindrical'``).
    dimension : int
        Number of active spatial dimensions discretized by the geometry.
    coordinate_name : str
        Symbol of the primary spatial coordinate (e.g., ``'x'`` or ``'r'``).
    p : int
        Radial symmetry factor (:math:`p = 0` planar, :math:`p = 1` cylindrical,
        :math:`p = 2` spherical).
    """

    _registry: ClassVar[dict[str, type[Geometry]]] = {}

    name: str = "geometry"
    dimension: int = 1
    coordinate_name: str = "x"
    p: int = 0

    def __init_subclass__(
        cls,
        name: str | None = None,
        geometry_name: str | None = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init_subclass__(**kwargs)
        resolved_name = name or geometry_name
        if resolved_name:
            cls._registry[resolved_name.lower()] = cls

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def area(self) -> float:
        r"""Active electrode surface area :math:`A` in :math:`\text{m}^2` or :math:`\text{cm}^2`."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    @property
    def surface_area(self) -> float:
        r"""Active electrode surface area :math:`A` (alias for :attr:`area`)."""
        return self.area

    @property
    def symmetry_factor(self) -> int:
        r"""Radial coordinate symmetry exponent :math:`p \in \{0, 1, 2\}`."""
        return self.p

    def validate_grid(self, grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D) -> np.ndarray:
        """Validate that a spatial grid satisfies the coordinate domain constraints.

        Parameters
        ----------
        grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D
            1D array or mesh of spatial coordinates.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            Validated 1D floating-point coordinate grid.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``grid`` is not 1D, has fewer than 3 points, is not strictly
            monotonically increasing, or violates radial domain bounds (:math:`r_0 > 0`).
        """
        arr = np.asarray(grid.nodes if isinstance(grid, Mesh1D) else grid, dtype=float)
        if arr.ndim != 1 or len(arr) < 3:
            raise ValueError("grid must be a 1D array with at least 3 points.")
        if np.any(np.diff(arr) <= 0.0):
            raise ValueError("grid points must be strictly monotonically increasing.")
        if self.p > 0 and arr[0] <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{self.__class__.__name__} requires strictly positive radial coordinates "
                f"(r0 = grid[0] > 0), got grid[0]={arr[0]}."
            )
        return arr

    @abstractmethod
    def laplacian(
        self,
        c: np.ndarray,
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D,
        bc_left: Any = None,
        bc_right: Any = None,
        t: float = 0.0,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""Evaluate the spatial Laplacian :math:`\nabla^2 c` at interior and boundary points.

        Parameters
        ----------
        c : np.ndarray
            1D concentration profile array of shape ``(N,)``.
        grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D
            1D spatial coordinate array or mesh of shape ``(N,)``.
        bc_left : BoundaryCondition, optional
            Boundary condition at the inner/left boundary (:math:`i = 0`).
        bc_right : BoundaryCondition, optional
            Boundary condition at the outer/right boundary (:math:`i = N - 1`).
        t : float, default 0.0
            Evaluation time in seconds for time-dependent boundary conditions.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            1D array of :math:`\nabla^2 c` values of shape ``(N,)``.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    def laplacian_matrix(
        self,
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D,
        bc_left: Any = None,
        bc_right: Any = None,
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        r"""Return banded matrix representation of :math:`\nabla^2` for implicit solvers.

        Constructs the tridiagonal finite-difference operator :math:`\mathbf{L}` in
        ``scipy.linalg.solve_banded`` ``(1, 1)`` format of shape ``(3, N)``, together
        with a boundary gradient scaling vector :math:`\mathbf{b}_{\text{scale}}` of
        shape ``(N,)`` such that for Neumann boundary gradients :math:`g_{\text{left}}`,
        :math:`g_{\text{right}}`:

        .. math::

            \nabla^2 \mathbf{c} = \mathbf{L}\mathbf{c}
                + \mathbf{b}_{\text{scale}} \odot [g_{\text{left}}, 0, \dots, 0, g_{\text{right}}]^T

        Parameters
        ----------
        grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D
            1D spatial coordinate array or mesh of shape ``(N,)``.
        bc_left : BoundaryCondition, optional
            Boundary condition at the left boundary (:math:`i = 0`).
        bc_right : BoundaryCondition, optional
            Boundary condition at the right boundary (:math:`i = N - 1`).

        Returns
        -------
        L_banded : np.ndarray
            Banded tridiagonal matrix of shape ``(3, N)`` where row 0 holds the
            superdiagonal, row 1 holds the main diagonal, and row 2 holds the subdiagonal.
        bc_scale : np.ndarray
            1D boundary gradient multiplier array of shape ``(N,)``.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    def surface_flux(
        self,
        c: np.ndarray,
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D,
        diffusivity: float,
        side: str = "left",
    ) -> float | np.ndarray:
        r"""Calculate normal interfacial diffusion flux :math:`J = -D (\partial c / \partial n)` at a boundary.

        Follows the electrode-normal convention where the unit normal :math:`\mathbf{n}`
        points from the boundary into the solution domain (:math:`+\hat{x}` or :math:`+\hat{r}`
        at the left boundary, and :math:`-\hat{x}` or :math:`-\hat{r}` at the right boundary).

        Parameters
        ----------
        c : np.ndarray
            Concentration profile of shape ``(N_x,)`` or time series of shape ``(N_t, N_x)``.
        grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D
            1D spatial coordinate array or mesh of shape ``(N_x,)``.
        diffusivity : float
            Species diffusion coefficient :math:`D > 0`.
        side : {'left', 'right'}, default 'left'
            Domain boundary at which to evaluate the normal flux.

        Returns
        -------
        float or np.ndarray
            Interfacial flux :math:`J` (scalar ``float`` if ``c`` is 1D, or 1D
            ``np.ndarray`` of shape ``(N_t,)`` if ``c`` is 2D).
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    def current(
        self,
        flux: float | np.ndarray,
        n_electrons: int = 1,
        side: Literal["left", "right"] = "left",
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D | None = None,
    ) -> float | np.ndarray:
        r"""Integrate normal flux over the active electrode surface to compute Faradaic current.

        Computes the total Faradaic current :math:`I = n F A J` according to IUPAC
        sign conventions (cathodic reduction :math:`I < 0` when reactant flux into
        solution is negative, :math:`J < 0`).

        Parameters
        ----------
        flux : float or np.ndarray
            Normal interfacial diffusion flux :math:`J` at the electrode surface.
        n_electrons : int, default 1
            Number of electrons transferred per reaction (:math:`n > 0`).
        side : {'left', 'right'}, default 'left'
            Domain boundary at which to compute the Faradaic current.
        grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D, optional
            Spatial grid coordinates used to determine surface area if coordinate-dependent.

        Returns
        -------
        float or np.ndarray
            Faradaic current :math:`I` in Amperes (:math:`\text{A}`).
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def _eval_1d_laplacian(
        self,
        c: np.ndarray,
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D,
        bc_left: Any = None,
        bc_right: Any = None,
        t: float = 0.0,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        """Evaluate 1D Cartesian or curvilinear radial Laplacian with 2nd-order stencils."""
        grid_arr = self.validate_grid(grid)
        c_arr = np.asarray(c, dtype=float)
        if c_arr.shape != grid_arr.shape:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Concentration array shape {c_arr.shape} must match grid shape {grid_arr.shape}."
            )

        n_pts = len(grid_arr)
        diffs = np.diff(grid_arr)
        is_uniform = (
            grid.is_uniform
            if isinstance(grid, Mesh1D)
            else bool(np.allclose(diffs, diffs[0], rtol=1e-5, atol=0.0))
        )
        p = self.p

        lap = np.empty(n_pts, dtype=float)

        # 1. Interior points (i = 1, ..., N - 2)
        if is_uniform:
            dr = float(diffs[0])
            inv_dr2 = 1.0 / (dr**2)
            d2c = (c_arr[2:] - 2.0 * c_arr[1:-1] + c_arr[:-2]) * inv_dr2
            if p == 0:
                lap[1:-1] = d2c
            else:
                dc = (c_arr[2:] - c_arr[:-2]) / (2.0 * dr)
                lap[1:-1] = d2c + (p / grid_arr[1:-1]) * dc
        else:
            hm1 = diffs[:-1]
            hi = diffs[1:]
            d2c = (2.0 / (hm1 + hi)) * (
                (c_arr[2:] - c_arr[1:-1]) / hi - (c_arr[1:-1] - c_arr[:-2]) / hm1
            )
            if p == 0:
                lap[1:-1] = d2c
            else:
                dc = (
                    (hm1**2) * (c_arr[2:] - c_arr[1:-1])
                    + (hi**2) * (c_arr[1:-1] - c_arr[:-2])
                ) / (hm1 * hi * (hm1 + hi))
                lap[1:-1] = d2c + (p / grid_arr[1:-1]) * dc

        # 2. Left boundary (i = 0)
        if bc_left is not None:
            btype_left = getattr(bc_left, "btype", None)
            if btype_left == "dirichlet":
                lap[0] = 0.0
            elif btype_left == "neumann":
                g_left = float(bc_left.evaluate(t))
                h0 = float(diffs[0])
                if is_uniform:
                    d2c_0 = (2.0 * c_arr[1] - 2.0 * c_arr[0] - 2.0 * h0 * g_left) / (
                        h0**2
                    )
                else:
                    d2c_0 = (2.0 / h0) * ((c_arr[1] - c_arr[0]) / h0 - g_left)
                lap[0] = d2c_0 if p == 0 else d2c_0 + (p / grid_arr[0]) * g_left
            else:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Unsupported left boundary condition type: {btype_left!r}."
                )
        else:
            # Pure operator evaluation at i = 0 using one-sided 2nd-order stencils
            h0, h1 = float(diffs[0]), float(diffs[1])
            dc_0 = (
                -(2.0 * h0 + h1) / (h0 * (h0 + h1)) * c_arr[0]
                + (h0 + h1) / (h0 * h1) * c_arr[1]
                - h0 / (h1 * (h0 + h1)) * c_arr[2]
            )
            if n_pts >= 4:
                d1 = grid_arr[1] - grid_arr[0]
                d2 = grid_arr[2] - grid_arr[0]
                d3 = grid_arr[3] - grid_arr[0]
                d2c_0 = -2.0 * (
                    -(d1 + d2 + d3) / (d1 * d2 * d3) * c_arr[0]
                    + (d2 + d3) / (d1 * (d1 - d2) * (d1 - d3)) * c_arr[1]
                    + (d1 + d3) / (d2 * (d2 - d1) * (d2 - d3)) * c_arr[2]
                    + (d1 + d2) / (d3 * (d3 - d1) * (d3 - d2)) * c_arr[3]
                )
            else:
                d2c_0 = (2.0 / (h0 + h1)) * (
                    (c_arr[2] - c_arr[1]) / h1 - (c_arr[1] - c_arr[0]) / h0
                )
            lap[0] = d2c_0 if p == 0 else d2c_0 + (p / grid_arr[0]) * dc_0

        # 3. Right boundary (i = N - 1)
        if bc_right is not None:
            btype_right = getattr(bc_right, "btype", None)
            if btype_right == "dirichlet":
                lap[-1] = 0.0
            elif btype_right == "neumann":
                g_right = float(bc_right.evaluate(t))
                h_end = float(diffs[-1])
                if is_uniform:
                    d2c_end = (
                        2.0 * c_arr[-2] - 2.0 * c_arr[-1] + 2.0 * h_end * g_right
                    ) / (h_end**2)
                else:
                    d2c_end = (2.0 / h_end) * (
                        g_right - (c_arr[-1] - c_arr[-2]) / h_end
                    )
                lap[-1] = d2c_end if p == 0 else d2c_end + (p / grid_arr[-1]) * g_right
            else:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Unsupported right boundary condition type: {btype_right!r}."
                )
        else:
            # Pure operator evaluation at i = N - 1 using one-sided 2nd-order stencils
            h_end, h_end2 = float(diffs[-1]), float(diffs[-2])
            dc_end = (
                (2.0 * h_end + h_end2) / (h_end * (h_end + h_end2)) * c_arr[-1]
                - (h_end + h_end2) / (h_end * h_end2) * c_arr[-2]
                + h_end / (h_end2 * (h_end + h_end2)) * c_arr[-3]
            )
            if n_pts >= 4:
                d1 = grid_arr[-2] - grid_arr[-1]
                d2 = grid_arr[-3] - grid_arr[-1]
                d3 = grid_arr[-4] - grid_arr[-1]
                d2c_end = -2.0 * (
                    -(d1 + d2 + d3) / (d1 * d2 * d3) * c_arr[-1]
                    + (d2 + d3) / (d1 * (d1 - d2) * (d1 - d3)) * c_arr[-2]
                    + (d1 + d3) / (d2 * (d2 - d1) * (d2 - d3)) * c_arr[-3]
                    + (d1 + d2) / (d3 * (d3 - d1) * (d3 - d2)) * c_arr[-4]
                )
            else:
                d2c_end = (2.0 / (h_end2 + h_end)) * (
                    (c_arr[-1] - c_arr[-2]) / h_end - (c_arr[-2] - c_arr[-3]) / h_end2
                )
            lap[-1] = d2c_end if p == 0 else d2c_end + (p / grid_arr[-1]) * dc_end

        return lap

    def _build_1d_laplacian_matrix(
        self,
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D,
        bc_left: Any = None,
        bc_right: Any = None,
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """Assemble banded tridiagonal Laplacian matrix and boundary source scaling."""
        grid_arr = self.validate_grid(grid)
        n_pts = len(grid_arr)
        diffs = np.diff(grid_arr)
        is_uniform = (
            grid.is_uniform
            if isinstance(grid, Mesh1D)
            else bool(np.allclose(diffs, diffs[0], rtol=1e-5, atol=0.0))
        )
        p = self.p

        l_banded = np.zeros((3, n_pts), dtype=float)
        bc_scale = np.zeros(n_pts, dtype=float)

        # Interior rows (i = 1, ..., N - 2)
        if is_uniform:
            dr = float(diffs[0])
            inv_dr2 = 1.0 / (dr**2)
            l_banded[1, 1:-1] = -2.0 * inv_dr2
            if p == 0:
                l_banded[0, 2:] = inv_dr2
                l_banded[2, :-2] = inv_dr2
            else:
                radial_term = p / (2.0 * grid_arr[1:-1] * dr)
                l_banded[0, 2:] = inv_dr2 + radial_term
                l_banded[2, :-2] = inv_dr2 - radial_term
        else:
            hm1 = diffs[:-1]
            hi = diffs[1:]
            denom_sum = hm1 + hi
            w2_lower = 2.0 / (hm1 * denom_sum)
            w2_diag = -2.0 / (hm1 * hi)
            w2_upper = 2.0 / (hi * denom_sum)

            if p == 0:
                l_banded[2, :-2] = w2_lower
                l_banded[1, 1:-1] = w2_diag
                l_banded[0, 2:] = w2_upper
            else:
                p_over_r = p / grid_arr[1:-1]
                w1_lower = -hi / (hm1 * denom_sum)
                w1_diag = (hi - hm1) / (hm1 * hi)
                w1_upper = hm1 / (hi * denom_sum)

                l_banded[2, :-2] = w2_lower + p_over_r * w1_lower
                l_banded[1, 1:-1] = w2_diag + p_over_r * w1_diag
                l_banded[0, 2:] = w2_upper + p_over_r * w1_upper

        # Left boundary (i = 0)
        btype_left = (
            getattr(bc_left, "btype", "neumann") if bc_left is not None else "neumann"
        )
        if btype_left == "dirichlet":
            l_banded[1, 0] = 0.0
            l_banded[0, 1] = 0.0
            bc_scale[0] = 0.0
        elif btype_left == "neumann":
            h0 = float(diffs[0])
            l_banded[1, 0] = -2.0 / (h0**2)
            l_banded[0, 1] = 2.0 / (h0**2)
            bc_scale[0] = -(2.0 / h0 - (p / grid_arr[0] if p > 0 else 0.0))
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported left boundary condition type: {btype_left!r}."
            )

        # Right boundary (i = N - 1)
        btype_right = (
            getattr(bc_right, "btype", "neumann") if bc_right is not None else "neumann"
        )
        if btype_right == "dirichlet":
            l_banded[1, -1] = 0.0
            l_banded[2, -2] = 0.0
            bc_scale[-1] = 0.0
        elif btype_right == "neumann":
            hm1_end = float(diffs[-1])
            l_banded[1, -1] = -2.0 / (hm1_end**2)
            l_banded[2, -2] = 2.0 / (hm1_end**2)
            bc_scale[-1] = 2.0 / hm1_end + (p / grid_arr[-1] if p > 0 else 0.0)
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported right boundary condition type: {btype_right!r}."
            )

        return l_banded, bc_scale

    def _eval_1d_surface_flux(
        self,
        c: np.ndarray,
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D,
        diffusivity: float,
        side: str = "left",
    ) -> float | np.ndarray:
        """Compute 2nd-order one-sided interfacial diffusion flux at left or right boundary."""
        if diffusivity <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Diffusivity must be positive (diffusivity > 0), got {diffusivity}."
            )
        if side not in ("left", "right"):
            raise ValueError(f"side must be 'left' or 'right', got {side!r}.")

        grid_arr = self.validate_grid(grid)
        c_arr = np.asarray(c, dtype=float)
        if c_arr.ndim not in (1, 2) or c_arr.shape[-1] != len(grid_arr):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Concentration array shape {c_arr.shape} is incompatible with grid of length {len(grid_arr)}."
            )

        diffs = np.diff(grid_arr)
        is_uniform = (
            grid.is_uniform
            if isinstance(grid, Mesh1D)
            else bool(np.allclose(diffs, diffs[0], rtol=1e-5, atol=0.0))
        )

        if side == "left":
            if is_uniform:
                dx = float(diffs[0])
                grad = (-3.0 * c_arr[..., 0] + 4.0 * c_arr[..., 1] - c_arr[..., 2]) / (
                    2.0 * dx
                )
            else:
                h0, h1 = float(diffs[0]), float(diffs[1])
                grad = (
                    -(2.0 * h0 + h1) / (h0 * (h0 + h1)) * c_arr[..., 0]
                    + (h0 + h1) / (h0 * h1) * c_arr[..., 1]
                    - h0 / (h1 * (h0 + h1)) * c_arr[..., 2]
                )
            flux = -diffusivity * grad
        else:
            if is_uniform:
                dx = float(diffs[0])
                grad = (
                    3.0 * c_arr[..., -1] - 4.0 * c_arr[..., -2] + c_arr[..., -3]
                ) / (2.0 * dx)
            else:
                hm1, hm2 = float(diffs[-1]), float(diffs[-2])
                grad = (
                    (2.0 * hm1 + hm2) / (hm1 * (hm1 + hm2)) * c_arr[..., -1]
                    - (hm1 + hm2) / (hm1 * hm2) * c_arr[..., -2]
                    + hm1 / (hm2 * (hm1 + hm2)) * c_arr[..., -3]
                )
            flux = diffusivity * grad

        if c_arr.ndim == 1:
            return float(flux)
        return np.asarray(flux, dtype=float)

    def _eval_1d_current(
        self,
        flux: float | np.ndarray,
        n_electrons: int = 1,
        area: float | None = None,
    ) -> float | np.ndarray:
        """Compute Faradaic current I = n * F * A * J."""
        if n_electrons <= 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Number of electrons n_electrons must be positive (n_electrons > 0), got {n_electrons}."
            )
        active_area = self.area if area is None else float(area)
        scale = float(n_electrons) * FARADAY * active_area
        if np.isscalar(flux):
            return float(scale * float(flux))  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        flux_arr = np.asarray(flux, dtype=float)
        if flux_arr.ndim == 0:
            return float(scale * float(flux_arr.item()))
        return scale * flux_arr

def validate_grid(self, grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D) -> np.ndarray:
    """Validate that a spatial grid satisfies the coordinate domain constraints.

    Parameters
    ----------
    grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D
        1D array or mesh of spatial coordinates.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        Validated 1D floating-point coordinate grid.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``grid`` is not 1D, has fewer than 3 points, is not strictly
        monotonically increasing, or violates radial domain bounds (:math:`r_0 > 0`).
    """
    arr = np.asarray(grid.nodes if isinstance(grid, Mesh1D) else grid, dtype=float)
    if arr.ndim != 1 or len(arr) < 3:
        raise ValueError("grid must be a 1D array with at least 3 points.")
    if np.any(np.diff(arr) <= 0.0):
        raise ValueError("grid points must be strictly monotonically increasing.")
    if self.p > 0 and arr[0] <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{self.__class__.__name__} requires strictly positive radial coordinates "
            f"(r0 = grid[0] > 0), got grid[0]={arr[0]}."
        )

class CylindricalGeometry(Geometry, name="cylindrical"):
    r"""1D cylindrical radial coordinate geometry (:math:`p = 1`).

    Models axisymmetric radial diffusion to or from a cylindrical wire or carbon
    fiber microelectrode of radius :math:`r_0 > 0` and length :math:`L > 0` across
    radial domain :math:`r \in [r_0, r_{\max}]`:

    .. math::

        \nabla^2 c = \frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial r^2} + \frac{1}{r} \frac{\partial c}{\partial r}
                   = \frac{1}{r} \frac{\partial}{\partial r} \left( r \frac{\partial c}{\partial r} \right)

    Neglecting end effects (:math:`L \gg r_0`), the active lateral electrode surface area
    at :math:`r = r_0` is:

    .. math::

        A = 2 \pi r_0 L, \quad I = n F A J

    Parameters
    ----------
    r0 : float, optional
        Cylinder radius :math:`r_0 > 0` in meters or cm. Defaults to ``1.0`` until
        bound to a radial coordinate grid.
    length : float, default 1.0
        Active cylinder length :math:`L > 0` in meters or cm.
    radius : float, optional
        Keyword alias for ``r0``.
    L : float, optional
        Keyword alias for ``length``.
    area : float, optional
        Explicit surface area override :math:`A > 0`. If None, computed analytically
        as :math:`A = 2 \pi r_0 L`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    name : str
        Geometry identifier (``'cylindrical'``).
    dimension : int
        Spatial dimension (``1``).
    coordinate_name : str
        Primary coordinate symbol (``'r'``).
    p : int
        Symmetry factor (``1``).
    r0 : float
        Cylinder radius :math:`r_0 > 0`.
    length : float
        Cylinder length :math:`L > 0`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``r0 <= 0``, ``length <= 0``, or ``area <= 0``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import numpy as np
    >>> from softpotato.geometry import CylindricalGeometry
    >>> geom = CylindricalGeometry(r0=5e-6, length=1e-2)
    >>> r = np.linspace(1.0, 5.0, 201)
    >>> c = np.log(r)  # Harmonic profile in cylindrical coordinates: ∇²(ln r) = 0
    >>> lap = geom.laplacian(c, r)
    >>> bool(np.max(np.abs(lap[1:-1])) < 1e-4)
    True
    """

    name: str = "cylindrical"
    dimension: int = 1
    coordinate_name: str = "r"
    p: int = 1

    def __init__(
        self,
        r0: float | None = None,
        length: float | None = None,
        *,
        radius: float | None = None,
        L: float | None = None,
        area: float | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if r0 is not None and radius is not None and r0 != radius:
            raise ValueError(
                "Cannot specify both 'r0' and 'radius' with different values."
            )
        if length is not None and L is not None and length != L:
            raise ValueError(
                "Cannot specify both 'length' and 'L' with different values."
            )

        resolved_r0 = radius if radius is not None else r0
        if resolved_r0 is not None:
            if resolved_r0 <= 0.0:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Cylinder radius r0 must be positive (r0 > 0), got {resolved_r0}."
                )
            self.r0 = float(resolved_r0)
            self._r0_explicit = True
        else:
            self.r0 = 1.0
            self._r0_explicit = False

        resolved_length = (
            1.0 if (length is None and L is None) else (L if L is not None else length)
        )
        assert resolved_length is not None
        if resolved_length <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Cylinder length must be positive (length > 0), got {resolved_length}."
            )
        self.length = float(resolved_length)

        if area is not None:
            if area <= 0.0:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Electrode area must be positive (area > 0), got {area}."
                )
            self._explicit_area: float | None = float(area)
        else:
            self._explicit_area = None

    @property
    def radius(self) -> float:
        r"""Cylinder radius :math:`r_0` (alias for :attr:`r0`)."""
        return self.r0

    @property
    def L(self) -> float:
        r"""Cylinder length :math:`L` (alias for :attr:`length`)."""
        return self.length

    @property
    def area(self) -> float:
        r"""Active lateral cylinder surface area :math:`A = 2\pi r_0 L`."""
        if self._explicit_area is not None:
            return self._explicit_area
        return 2.0 * math.pi * self.r0 * self.length

    def validate_grid(self, grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D) -> np.ndarray:
        """Validate radial grid bounds (:math:`r_0 > 0`) and infer ``r0`` if not explicitly set."""
        arr = super().validate_grid(grid)
        if not self._r0_explicit:
            self.r0 = float(arr[0])
        return arr

    def laplacian(
        self,
        c: np.ndarray,
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D,
        bc_left: Any = None,
        bc_right: Any = None,
        t: float = 0.0,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""Evaluate the cylindrical Laplacian :math:`\nabla^2 c = \frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial r^2} + \frac{1}{r}\frac{\partial c}{\partial r}`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        c : np.ndarray
            1D concentration array of shape ``(N,)``.
        grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D
            1D radial coordinate grid :math:`r \in [r_0, r_{\max}]` of shape ``(N,)`` with :math:`r_0 > 0`.
        bc_left : BoundaryCondition, optional
            Inner boundary condition at :math:`r = r_0`.
        bc_right : BoundaryCondition, optional
            Outer boundary condition at :math:`r = r_{\max}`.
        t : float, default 0.0
            Time in seconds for evaluating time-dependent boundary conditions.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            1D array of :math:`\nabla^2 c` values of shape ``(N,)``.
        """
        return self._eval_1d_laplacian(c, grid, bc_left=bc_left, bc_right=bc_right, t=t)

    def laplacian_matrix(
        self,
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D,
        bc_left: Any = None,
        bc_right: Any = None,
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        r"""Assemble banded matrix representation of the cylindrical Laplacian :math:`\nabla^2`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D
            1D radial grid :math:`r` of shape ``(N,)`` with :math:`r_0 > 0`.
        bc_left : BoundaryCondition, optional
            Inner boundary condition at :math:`r = r_0`.
        bc_right : BoundaryCondition, optional
            Outer boundary condition at :math:`r = r_{\max}`.

        Returns
        -------
        L_banded : np.ndarray
            Banded tridiagonal operator matrix of shape ``(3, N)``.
        bc_scale : np.ndarray
            Boundary gradient scaling vector of shape ``(N,)``.
        """
        return self._build_1d_laplacian_matrix(grid, bc_left=bc_left, bc_right=bc_right)

    def surface_flux(
        self,
        c: np.ndarray,
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D,
        diffusivity: float,
        side: str = "left",
    ) -> float | np.ndarray:
        r"""Calculate normal interfacial diffusion flux :math:`J = -D (\partial c / \partial n)`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        c : np.ndarray
            Concentration array of shape ``(N_r,)`` or ``(N_t, N_r)``.
        grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D
            1D radial grid :math:`r` of shape ``(N_r,)`` with :math:`r_0 > 0`.
        diffusivity : float
            Species diffusion coefficient :math:`D > 0`.
        side : {'left', 'right'}, default 'left'
            Boundary side at which to evaluate the normal flux.

        Returns
        -------
        float or np.ndarray
            Normal interfacial diffusion flux :math:`J`.
        """
        return self._eval_1d_surface_flux(c, grid, diffusivity=diffusivity, side=side)

    def current(
        self,
        flux: float | np.ndarray,
        n_electrons: int = 1,
        side: Literal["left", "right"] = "left",
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D | None = None,
    ) -> float | np.ndarray:
        r"""Integrate normal flux over the cylindrical electrode surface :math:`I = n F A J`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        flux : float or np.ndarray
            Interfacial diffusion flux :math:`J`.
        n_electrons : int, default 1
            Number of electrons transferred per reaction (:math:`n > 0`).
        side : {'left', 'right'}, default 'left'
            Domain boundary at which to compute the Faradaic current.
        grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D, optional
            Spatial grid coordinates used to determine outer boundary area when ``side='right'``.

        Returns
        -------
        float or np.ndarray
            Faradaic current :math:`I` in Amperes (:math:`\text{A}`).
        """
        if side == "right" and grid is not None and self._explicit_area is None:
            r_right = float(np.asarray(grid)[-1])
            area = 2.0 * math.pi * r_right * self.length
            return self._eval_1d_current(flux, n_electrons=n_electrons, area=area)
        return self._eval_1d_current(flux, n_electrons=n_electrons)

def current(
    self,
    flux: float | np.ndarray,
    n_electrons: int = 1,
    side: Literal["left", "right"] = "left",
    grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D | None = None,
) -> float | np.ndarray:
    r"""Integrate normal flux over the cylindrical electrode surface :math:`I = n F A J`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    flux : float or np.ndarray
        Interfacial diffusion flux :math:`J`.
    n_electrons : int, default 1
        Number of electrons transferred per reaction (:math:`n > 0`).
    side : {'left', 'right'}, default 'left'
        Domain boundary at which to compute the Faradaic current.
    grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D, optional
        Spatial grid coordinates used to determine outer boundary area when ``side='right'``.

    Returns
    -------
    float or np.ndarray
        Faradaic current :math:`I` in Amperes (:math:`\text{A}`).
    """
    if side == "right" and grid is not None and self._explicit_area is None:
        r_right = float(np.asarray(grid)[-1])
        area = 2.0 * math.pi * r_right * self.length
        return self._eval_1d_current(flux, n_electrons=n_electrons, area=area)
    return self._eval_1d_current(flux, n_electrons=n_electrons)

>>> from softpotato.geometry import PlanarGeometry
>>> geom = PlanarGeometry(area=0.5)
>>> x = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 21)
>>> c = x**2  # d²(x²)/dx² = 2.0 everywhere

class PlanarGeometry(Geometry, name="planar"):
    r"""1D planar Cartesian coordinate geometry (:math:`p = 0`).

    Models semi-infinite or finite linear diffusion perpendicular to a flat macroelectrode
    along spatial coordinate :math:`x \in [x_0, x_{\max}]`:

    .. math::

        \nabla^2 c = \frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial x^2}

    The active electrode surface area is constant (:math:`A`), yielding Faradaic current:

    .. math::

        I = n F A J, \quad J_{\text{left}} = -D \left.\frac{\partial c}{\partial x}\right|_{x_0}

    Parameters
    ----------
    area : float, default 1.0
        Active electrode surface area :math:`A` in :math:`\text{m}^2` or :math:`\text{cm}^2`
        (:math:`A > 0`).

    Attributes
    ----------
    name : str
        Geometry identifier (``'planar'``).
    dimension : int
        Spatial dimension (``1``).
    coordinate_name : str
        Primary coordinate symbol (``'x'``).
    p : int
        Symmetry factor (``0``).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``area <= 0``.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> import numpy as np
    >>> from softpotato.geometry import PlanarGeometry
    >>> geom = PlanarGeometry(area=0.5)
    >>> x = np.linspace(0.0, 1.0, 21)
    >>> c = x**2  # d²(x²)/dx² = 2.0 everywhere
    >>> lap = geom.laplacian(c, x)
    >>> bool(np.allclose(lap, 2.0))
    True
    >>> flux = geom.surface_flux(x, x, diffusivity=1e-5, side="left")
    >>> round(flux, 8)
    -1e-05
    """

    name: str = "planar"
    dimension: int = 1
    coordinate_name: str = "x"
    p: int = 0

    def __init__(self, area: float = 1.0) -> None:
        if area <= 0.0:
            raise ValueError(f"Electrode area must be positive (area > 0), got {area}.")
        self._area = float(area)

    @property
    def area(self) -> float:
        r"""Active electrode surface area :math:`A`."""
        return self._area

    def laplacian(
        self,
        c: np.ndarray,
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D,
        bc_left: Any = None,
        bc_right: Any = None,
        t: float = 0.0,
    ) -> np.ndarray:
        r"""Evaluate the 1D Cartesian Laplacian :math:`\nabla^2 c = \partial^2 c / \partial x^2`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        c : np.ndarray
            1D concentration array of shape ``(N,)``.
        grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D
            1D spatial grid :math:`x` of shape ``(N,)``.
        bc_left : BoundaryCondition, optional
            Left boundary condition at :math:`x_0`.
        bc_right : BoundaryCondition, optional
            Right boundary condition at :math:`x_{N-1}`.
        t : float, default 0.0
            Time in seconds for evaluating time-dependent boundary conditions.

        Returns
        -------
        np.ndarray
            1D array of :math:`\partial^2 c / \partial x^2` values of shape ``(N,)``.
        """
        return self._eval_1d_laplacian(c, grid, bc_left=bc_left, bc_right=bc_right, t=t)

    def laplacian_matrix(
        self,
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D,
        bc_left: Any = None,
        bc_right: Any = None,
    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        r"""Assemble banded matrix representation of :math:`\partial^2 / \partial x^2`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D
            1D spatial grid :math:`x` of shape ``(N,)``.
        bc_left : BoundaryCondition, optional
            Left boundary condition at :math:`x_0`.
        bc_right : BoundaryCondition, optional
            Right boundary condition at :math:`x_{N-1}`.

        Returns
        -------
        L_banded : np.ndarray
            Banded tridiagonal operator matrix of shape ``(3, N)``.
        bc_scale : np.ndarray
            Boundary gradient scaling vector of shape ``(N,)``.
        """
        return self._build_1d_laplacian_matrix(grid, bc_left=bc_left, bc_right=bc_right)

    def surface_flux(
        self,
        c: np.ndarray,
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D,
        diffusivity: float,
        side: str = "left",
    ) -> float | np.ndarray:
        r"""Calculate normal interfacial diffusion flux :math:`J = -D (\partial c / \partial n)`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        c : np.ndarray
            Concentration array of shape ``(N_x,)`` or ``(N_t, N_x)``.
        grid : np.ndarray or Mesh1D
            1D spatial grid :math:`x` of shape ``(N_x,)``.
        diffusivity : float
            Species diffusion coefficient :math:`D > 0`.
        side : {'left', 'right'}, default 'left'
            Boundary side at which to evaluate the normal flux.

        Returns
        -------
        float or np.ndarray
            Normal interfacial diffusion flux :math:`J`.
        """
        return self._eval_1d_surface_flux(c, grid, diffusivity=diffusivity, side=side)

    def current(
        self,
        flux: float | np.ndarray,
        n_electrons: int = 1,
        side: Literal["left", "right"] = "left",
        grid: np.ndarray | Mesh1D | None = None,
    ) -> float | np.ndarray:
        r"""Compute Faradaic current :math:`I = n F A J`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        flux : float or np.ndarray
            Interfacial diffusion flux :math:`J`.
        n_electrons : int, default 1
            Number of electrons transferred per reaction (:math:`n > 0`).
        side : {'left', 'right'}, default 'left'
            Domain boundary at which to compute the Faradaic current.
        grid : np.ndarray, optional
            Spatial grid coordinates (unused for planar geometry).

        Returns
        -------
        float or np.ndarray
            Faradaic current :math:`I` in Amperes (:math:`\text{A}`).
        """
        return self._eval_1d_current(flux, n_electrons=n_electrons)

1D spherical radial coordinate geometry (\(p = 2\)).

Models radial diffusion to or from a spherical microelectrode, hanging mercury drop electrode (HMDE), or hemispherical microelectrode on an insulating plane across radial domain \(r \in [r_0, r_{\max}]\) with \(r_0 > 0\):

\[ \nabla^2 c = \frac{\partial^2 c}{\partial r^2} + \frac{2}{r} \frac{\partial c}{\partial r} = \frac{1}{r^2} \frac{\partial}{\partial r} \left( r^2 \frac{\partial c}{\partial r} \right) \]

The active electrode surface area at \(r = r_0\) is:

  • Full sphere (hemisphere=False): \(A = 4 \pi r_0^2\)
  • Hemisphere (hemisphere=True): \(A = 2 \pi r_0^2\)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default r0 float

Electrode radius \(r_0 > 0\) in meters or cm. Defaults to 1.0 until bound to a radial coordinate grid.

None hemisphere bool

If True, computes surface area for a hemisphere (\(A = 2 \pi r_0^2\)) instead of a full sphere (\(A = 4 \pi r_0^2\)).

False radius float

Keyword alias for r0.

None mode ('sphere', 'hemisphere')

Alternative specification of full sphere vs. hemisphere geometry.

'sphere' area float

Explicit surface area override \(A > 0\). If None, computed analytically from \(r_0\) and hemisphere.
