docs.title: 1. Goal¶
docs.text: Simulate a diffusion-controlled potential-step (chronoamperometry) experiment at a planar electrode, verify the classic $t^{-1/2}$ Cottrell decay, and extract the diffusion coefficient $D$ using both analyze_cottrell() and fit_cottrell().

docs.title: 2. Physical Setup¶
docs.text: We consider a one-electron reduction $\text{Ox} + e^- \rightleftharpoons \text{Red}$ at a planar disk electrode ($A = 7.07 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2$, 3 mm diameter) under Nernstian equilibrium ($E^{0\prime} = 0.0\text{ V}$). Stepping the potential to $E_{\text{step}} = -0.4\text{ V}$ drives the surface concentration of $\text{Ox}$ to essentially zero.

docs.title: 3. Simulation¶
docs.text: We instantiate Chronoamperometry and call simulate(), which builds an adaptive stretched spatial mesh and integrates the diffusion PDE.

docs.title: 4. Diagnostics & Plots¶
docs.text: The Cottrell equation predicts that $I(t)$ is linear in $t^{-1/2}$ with zero intercept. We use analyze_cottrell() + plot_cottrell(), and cross-check with fit_cottrell() for 95% confidence intervals.

docs.title: 5. Key Takeaways¶
docs.text:
• For a large overpotential step at a planar electrode, $I(t) = -\frac{n F A D^{1/2} c^*}{\sqrt{\pi t}}$ (IUPAC cathodic sign).
  • Plotting $I$ vs. $t^{-1/2}$ (plot_cottrell()) yields a straight line whose slope directly gives $D$.
  • Next: Compare Planar, Spherical & Cylindrical Cottrell or read the Step Techniques Guide.

docs.title: Chronoamperometry Across Geometries: Planar, Spherical & Cylindrical¶
1. Goal¶
docs.text: Compare potential-step current density transients across PlanarGeometry, SphericalGeometry, and CylindricalGeometry, and observe how radial diffusion produces a non-zero steady-state current at spherical microelectrodes.

docs.title: 2. Physical Setup¶
docs.text:
We use the same redox couple ($D = 10^{-9}\text{ m}^2/\text{s}$, $c^* = 1\text{ mM}$, $n = 1$) and apply a $5\text{ s}$ step to $-0.4\text{ V}$ at:

  1. A planar macroelectrode ($A = 7.07 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2$).
  2. A spherical microelectrode ($r_0 = 25\,\mu\text{m}$).
  3. A cylindrical wire microelectrode ($r_0 = 25\,\mu\text{m}$, $L = 1\text{ cm}$).

docs.title: 3. Simulation¶
docs.text: We run simulate() for each geometry and normalize the current by each electrode's active surface area ($j = I / A$) so the flux densities can be compared directly.

docs.title: 4. Diagnostics & Plots¶
docs.text: We compare the simulated current densities against the exact analytical expressions (cottrell(), cottrell_spherical(), cottrell_cylinder()) and mark the spherical steady-state limit $j_{\text{ss}} = -n F D c^* / r_0$.

docs.title: 5. Key Takeaways¶
docs.text:
• Planar current density decays monotonically as $t^{-1/2} \to 0$.
  • Spherical diffusion accesses a 3D hemispherical volume, converging to a finite steady-state current density $j_{\text{ss}} = -n F D c^* / r_0$.
  • Cylindrical diffusion decays much more slowly than planar ($\sim 1/\ln t$), sitting between planar and spherical behavior.
  • Next: See CV on a Spherical Microelectrode or the Mass Transport Concepts.

docs.title: 1. Goal¶
docs.text: Simulate single- and multi-cycle Cyclic Voltammetry (CyclicVoltammetry), inspect peak positions and currents with find_peaks() and plot_summary(), and run a scan-rate sweep with simulate_sweep().

docs.text: We model a quasi-reversible one-electron couple ($E^{0\prime} = 0.0\text{ V}$, $k^0 = 10^{-3}\text{ m/s}$, $\alpha = 0.5$) at a 3 mm planar disk electrode.

docs.title: 3. Simulation¶

docs.title: 5. Key Takeaways¶
docs.text:
• CyclicVoltammetry(..., n_cycles=2) handles piecewise switching events automatically.
  • find_peaks() refines peak potentials parabolically and reports $\Delta E_p$, $E_{1/2}$, and $|I_{pa}/I_{pc}|$.
  • simulate_sweep() + plot_sweep() make multi-scan-rate studies one-liners.

docs.text: Simulate Sampled-Current Voltammetry (SampledCurrentVoltammetry), Differential Pulse Voltammetry (DifferentialPulseVoltammetry), Square-Wave Voltammetry (SquareWaveVoltammetry), and Chronopotentiometry (Chronopotentiometry) with automatic Sand transition time analysis.

docs.title: 2. Physical Setup¶
docs.text: We use a planar 3 mm disk electrode with $E^{0\prime} = 0.0\text{ V}$, $D = 10^{-9}\text{ m}^2/\text{s}$, $c^* = 1\text{ mM}$, and $k^0 = 10^{-3}\text{ m/s}$.

docs.title: 3. Simulation¶
docs.text: We simulate all four techniques using simulate(). For Chronopotentiometry, we apply a constant cathodic current $I = -15\,\mu\text{A}$ for $4\text{ s}$.

docs.title: 4. Diagnostics & Plots¶
docs.text: We visualize the sampled/differential voltammograms with plot_scv(), plot_dpv(), and plot_swv(), and compare the simulated CP transition time against sand_transition_time().

docs.title: 5. Key Takeaways¶
docs.text:
• SCV produces sigmoidal steady-like waves at fixed sampling times $\tau$.
  • DPV and SWV compute differential currents ($\Delta I$) that peak sharply near $E^{0\prime}$, offering superior sensitivity.
  • CP holds constant current until surface concentration depletes at the Sand transition time $\tau$, where $E(t)$ drops sharply.
  • Next: Read the Pulse Voltammetry Guide or Step Techniques Guide.

docs.title: Rotating Disk Electrode (RDE): Levich & Koutecký–Levich Analysis¶
1. Goal¶
docs.text: Simulate hydrodynamic voltammetry at a Rotating Disk Electrode (simulate_rde_sweep()), verify the Levich equation ($I_{\text{lim}} \propto \omega^{1/2}$) for a reversible couple, and extract $k^0$ and $D$ from a quasi-reversible couple via Koutecký–Levich analysis.

docs.title: 2. Physical Setup¶
docs.text: We model a 5 mm diameter RDE ($A = 1.96 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}^2$) in aqueous electrolyte ($\nu = 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2/\text{s}$) across rotation rates $400, 900, 1600, 2500\text{ rpm}$.

docs.title: 3. Simulation¶
docs.text: We run simulate_rde_sweep() for both the reversible (nernst) and quasi-reversible (bv_quasi) cases using the convective-diffusion model.

docs.title: 4. Diagnostics & Plots¶
docs.text: We plot the rotation-rate series (plot_sweep()), the Levich plot (plot_levich()), and the Koutecký–Levich plot (plot_koutecky_levich() at $E = -0.15\text{ V}$).

docs.title: 5. Key Takeaways¶
docs.text:
• Forced convection establishes a thin steady Nernst diffusion layer $\delta_N \propto \omega^{-1/2}$, yielding sigmoidal waves.
  • Levich plots ($|I_{\text{lim}}|$ vs. $\omega^{1/2}$) pass through the origin and measure $D$.
  • Koutecký–Levich plots ($1/|I|$ vs. $\omega^{-1/2}$) separate mass transport (slope) from finite electron-transfer kinetics (intercept $1/|I_K|$).
  • Next: Read the RDE User Guide.

docs.title: User Guide: Techniques & Waveforms
docs.text: The softpotato.techniques module provides a high-level simulation pipeline that handles spatial meshing, boundary conditions, piecewise event-aware time integration, and Faradaic current extraction in a single simulate() call.

docs.title: The simulate() Pipeline
docs.text:
Every simulation follows the same three-step pattern:

  1. Define the chemical system: create Species (ordered [ox, red] for \(\text{Ox} + n e^- \rightarrow \text{Red}\)) and optional electrode kinetics (ButlerVolmer, MarcusHushChidsey, or NernstianEquilibrium).
  2. Choose a technique: instantiate a waveform generator such as CyclicVoltammetry, Chronoamperometry, SquareWaveVoltammetry, RotatingDiskElectrode, or CustomWaveform.
  3. Run and visualize: call simulate(technique, [ox, red], geometry=PlanarGeometry(area), kinetics=kinetics) and pass the returned TechniqueResult to plot_result(result) or plot_summary(result).

Units Convention (SI)

All softpotato.techniques simulations use consistent SI units:

  • Length: \(\text{m}\) (Area: \(\text{m}^2\))
  • Time: \(\text{s}\)
  • Potential: \(\text{V}\)
  • Current: \(\text{A}\)
  • Concentration: \(\text{mol}/\text{m}^3\) (\(1\text{ mol}/\text{m}^3 = 1\text{ mM}\))
  • Diffusion coefficient: \(\text{m}^2/\text{s}\) (\(10^{-9}\text{ m}^2/\text{s} = 10^{-5}\text{ cm}^2/\text{s}\))
  • Heterogeneous rate constant: \(\text{m}/\text{s}\) (\(10^{-3}\text{ m}/\text{s} = 0.1\text{ cm}/\text{s}\))

docs.title: Parameter Sweeps with simulate_sweep()
docs.text:
To run a series of simulations across scan rates, step potentials, or any other parameter, pass a list, dictionary, or factory callable + values to simulate_sweep():

results = simulate_sweep(
    lambda v: CyclicVoltammetry(E_start=0.4, E_vertex1=-0.4, E_vertex2=0.4, scan_rate=v),
    [ox, red],
    values=[0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5],
    geometry=geometry,
    kinetics=kinetics,
)

Overlay the resulting traces with plot_sweep(results).

docs.title: Curve Fitting & Parameter Estimation (softpotato.analytical.fitting)
docs.text: The softpotato.analytical.fitting submodule wraps SciPy's least-squares optimizers with physical parameter bounds, Student's \(t\) confidence intervals, covariance/correlation matrices, and goodness-of-fit diagnostics (\(R^2\), adjusted \(R^2\), RMSE, and reduced \(\chi_\nu^2\)).

docs.title: Specialized & General-Purpose Fitters
docs.text: Function Model / Equation Primary Extracted Parameters fit_cottrell Planar Cottrell CA transient Diffusion coefficient \(D\), background \(I_{\text{bg}}\) fit_randles_sevcik CV peak current \(I_p\) vs. scan rate \(v\) Diffusion coefficient \(D\), slope, intercept fit_secm_approach SECM feedback approach curve Insulator ratio \(RG\), zero-distance offset \(d_{\text{offset}}\), optional \(\kappa\) fit_levich RDE limiting current \(I_L\) vs. \(\omega\) Diffusion coefficient \(D\), Levich constant \(B\) fit_koutecky_levich RDE mixed-control \(I\) vs. \(\omega\) Kinetic current \(I_K\), \(k_{\text{rate}}\), \(D\), Levich \(B\) fit_tafel High-overpotential \(\eta\) vs. \(\log_{10}\|I\|\) Exchange current \(I_0\), Tafel slope \(b\), \(\alpha\), optional \(k^0\) fit_butler_volmer Full-range \(I\) vs. \(\eta\) \(I_0\), \(\alpha\), optional \(k^0\) fit_microdisc_transient Shoup–Szabo / Mahon–Oldham UME transient \(D\) or microdisc radius \(a\) fit_linear Weighted or ordinary \(y = m x + b\) Slope \(m\), intercept \(b\) fit_curve Any user-defined callable f(x, *params) Custom param_names with bounds & uncertainty

docs.title: The FitResult Container
docs.text:
Every fitter returns a FitResult (or specialized subclass such as CottrellFitResult, RandlesSevcikFitResult, or SECMApproachFitResult) exposing:

  • params, stderr, confidence_intervals: dictionaries keyed by parameter name
  • covariance, correlation: parameter covariance and normalized correlation matrices
  • r_squared, r_squared_adj, rmse, chi2_reduced: goodness-of-fit metrics
  • y_fit, residuals, success, message, nfev: model predictions and optimizer status

docs.title: Full Runnable Script
docs.text:
"""User Guide: Curve Fitting & Parameter Estimation.

Demonstrates softpotato.analytical.fitting:
1. fit_cottrell() — extract D from chronoamperometry transients
2. fit_randles_sevcik() — extract D from CV peak current vs. scan rate
3. fit_secm_approach() — extract RG and d_offset from SECM approach curves
4. fit_curve() — general-purpose bounded nonlinear least-squares regression
"""

import numpy as np

from softpotato import analytical as spa

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)

n = 1
D_true = 1.0e-9  # m^2/s
c_bulk = 1.0  # mol/m^3
area = 7.07e-6  # m^2
T = 298.15  # K

# 1. fit_cottrell()
t_ca = np.linspace(0.05, 3.0, 60)
i_ca = spa.cottrell(t_ca, n=n, D=D_true, c_bulk=c_bulk, area=area) + rng.normal(
    0.0, 2.0e-7, size=t_ca.size
)
ca_fit = spa.fit_cottrell(t_ca, i_ca, n=n, area=area, c_bulk=c_bulk)
print(
    f"fit_cottrell:      D = {ca_fit.d:.3e} +/- {ca_fit.d_stderr:.2e} m^2/s, "
    f"R^2 = {ca_fit.r_squared:.5f}"
)

# 2. fit_randles_sevcik()
v_cv = np.array([0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0])
ip_cv = spa.randles_sevcik(v_cv, c_bulk=c_bulk, D=D_true, area=area, n=n, T=T)
ip_cv += rng.normal(0.0, 1.0e-6, size=v_cv.size)
rs_fit = spa.fit_randles_sevcik(v_cv, ip_cv, n=n, area=area, c_bulk=c_bulk, T=T)
print(
    f"fit_randles_sevcik: D = {rs_fit.d:.3e} +/- {rs_fit.d_stderr:.2e} m^2/s, "
    f"R^2 = {rs_fit.r_squared:.5f}"
)

# 3. fit_secm_approach()
a_ume = 12.5e-6
d_secm = np.linspace(3.0e-6, 45.0e-6, 50)
L_true = (d_secm - 0.6e-6) / a_ume
it_secm = spa.secm_approach_positive_feedback(L_true, RG=5.0) + rng.normal(
    0.0, 0.02, size=d_secm.size
)
secm_fit = spa.fit_secm_approach(d_secm, it_secm, substrate="conducting", a=a_ume)
print(
    f"fit_secm_approach: RG = {secm_fit.rg:.2f}, "
    f"d_offset = {secm_fit.d_offset * 1e6:.2f} um, R^2 = {secm_fit.r_squared:.5f}"
)


# 4. fit_curve() — custom bounded nonlinear model (exponential RC decay)
def rc_decay(t_arr: np.ndarray, i0: float, tau: float) -> np.ndarray:
    return i0 * np.exp(-t_arr / tau)


t_rc = np.linspace(0.0, 0.05, 80)
i_rc = rc_decay(t_rc, 5.0e-4, 0.012) + rng.normal(0.0, 5.0e-6, size=t_rc.size)
rc_fit = spa.fit_curve(
    rc_decay,
    t_rc,
    i_rc,
    p0=[4.0e-4, 0.01],
    bounds=([0.0, 1e-6], [1.0, 1.0]),
    param_names=["I0", "tau"],
)
print(
    f"fit_curve:         I0 = {rc_fit.params['I0'] * 1e6:.1f} uA, "
    f"tau = {rc_fit.params['tau'] * 1e3:.2f} ms, R^2 = {rc_fit.r_squared:.5f}"
)

docs.title: Analytical Models (softpotato.analytical)
docs.text:
The softpotato.analytical package provides closed-form solutions, asymptotic expansions, and empirical electrochemical models for rapid baseline calculations and solver benchmarking.

Consistent Units

All functions in softpotato.analytical are unit-agnostic as long as length units are consistent across D, area, c_bulk, nu, and electrode radius a (for example, all SI: \(\text{m}\), \(\text{m}^2\), \(\text{mol}/\text{m}^3\); or all CGS: \(\text{cm}\), \(\text{cm}^2\), \(\text{mol}/\text{cm}^3\)).

docs.title: softpotato.analytical.step — Potential & Current Steps
docs.text:
• cottrell, cottrell_spherical, cottrell_cylinder, cottrell_step: Chronoamperometric current transients at planar, spherical, and cylindrical electrodes.
  • anson: Chronocoulometric charge \(Q(t)\) for planar potential steps.
  • sand, sand_transition_time, sand_potential: Galvanostatic chronopotentiometry transition time \(\tau\) and \(E(t)\) response.
  • step_concentration_profile, step_flux_profile: Exact error-function spatial concentration \(c(x, t)\) and interfacial flux profiles.

docs.title: softpotato.analytical.hydrodynamics — RDE & RRDE
docs.text:
• levich, levich_constant, nernst_diffusion_layer: Levich limiting current \(I_L\), Levich constant \(B\), and Nernst diffusion layer thickness \(\delta_N\).
  • koutecky_levich, koutecky_levich_analysis: Mixed kinetic/mass-transport RDE current and regression.
  • rpm_to_rad_s, rad_s_to_rpm: Angular velocity conversions (\(\omega = 2\pi \cdot \text{rpm} / 60\)).
  • collection_efficiency, ring_limiting_current, ring_collection_current, shielding_factor, rotating_ring_disk: Albery–Bruckenstein rotating ring-disk electrode (RRDE) equations.

docs.title: softpotato.analytical.kinetics — Interfacial Kinetics
docs.text:
• nernst, nernst_potential, nernst_ratio, nernst_equilibrium_concentrations: Equilibrium potential and surface concentration ratios.
  • exchange_current, exchange_current_density, charge_transfer_resistance: \(I_0\), \(j_0\), and \(R_{\text{ct}}\).
  • butler_volmer, butler_volmer_current_density, butler_volmer_linear: Full and low-overpotential linearized Butler–Volmer equations.
  • tafel, tafel_slope, tafel_overpotential, tafel_analysis: High-field Tafel kinetics.

docs.title: softpotato.analytical.voltammetry — Voltammetric Diagnostics
docs.text:
• randles_sevcik, randles_sevcik_irreversible, randles_sevcik_quasi: Reversible, irreversible, and quasi-reversible CV peak currents.
  • nicholson_psi, nicholson_delta_ep, nicholson_rate_constant: Nicholson working curve relating \(\Delta E_p\) to \(\Psi\) and \(k^0\).
  • matsuda_ayabe, matsuda_ayabe_lambda, peak_potential_irreversible: Dimensionless reversibility parameter \(\Lambda\) and regime classification.

docs.title: softpotato.analytical.microelectrodes — Ultramicroelectrodes (UMEs)
docs.text:
• microdisc_limiting_current, microhemisphere_limiting_current, microsphere_limiting_current, microband_limiting_current: Steady-state UME limiting currents.
  • microdisc_transient, mahon_oldham_transient: Shoup–Szabo and Mahon–Oldham microdisc chronoamperometric transients.

docs.title: softpotato.analytical.secm — Scanning Electrochemical Microscopy
docs.text:
• secm_approach_positive_feedback, secm_approach_negative_feedback, secm_approach_curve: Normalized SECM tip current \(I_T(L)\) for conducting, insulating, and finite-kinetics substrates.
  • secm_limiting_current_infinite, secm_tip_current: Steady-state tip current in bulk and dimensional approach currents.

docs.title: Full Runnable Script
docs.text:
"""User Guide: Analytical Models across softpotato.analytical Submodules.

Demonstrates closed-form equations in:
1. step: cottrell, anson, sand_transition_time
2. hydrodynamics: levich, koutecky_levich, collection_efficiency
3. kinetics: nernst, butler_volmer, tafel_slope
4. voltammetry: randles_sevcik, nicholson_psi, matsuda_ayabe
5. microelectrodes: microdisc_limiting_current, microdisc_transient
6. secm: secm_approach_positive_feedback, secm_approach_negative_feedback, secm_approach_curve
"""

import numpy as np

from softpotato.analytical import (
    hydrodynamics,
    kinetics,
    microelectrodes,
    secm,
    step,
    voltammetry,
)

# Consistent SI units
n = 1
D = 1.0e-9  # m^2/s
c_bulk = 1.0  # mol/m^3 (= 1 mM)
area = 7.07e-6  # m^2 (3 mm disk)
nu = 1.0e-6  # m^2/s (water)
T = 298.15  # K

# 1. Step techniques
t = np.array([0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0])
i_cott = step.cottrell(t, n=n, D=D, c_bulk=c_bulk, area=area)
q_anson = step.anson(t, n=n, D=D, c_bulk=c_bulk, area=area)
tau_sand = step.sand_transition_time(I=4.0e-5, n=n, D=D, c_bulk=c_bulk, area=area)
print(
    f"Step: Cottrell I(1s) = {i_cott[2] * 1e6:.2f} uA, "
    f"Anson Q(1s) = {q_anson[2] * 1e6:.2f} uC, Sand tau = {tau_sand:.3f} s"
)

# 2. Hydrodynamics (RDE & RRDE)
i_lev = hydrodynamics.levich(rpm=1600, n=n, D=D, c_bulk=c_bulk, area=area, nu=nu)
i_kl = hydrodynamics.koutecky_levich(
    omega=hydrodynamics.rpm_to_rad_s(1600),
    n=n,
    D=D,
    c_bulk=c_bulk,
    area=area,
    nu=nu,
    i_k=5.0e-4,
)
n_coll = hydrodynamics.collection_efficiency(r1=2.5e-3, r2=2.75e-3, r3=3.75e-3)
print(
    f"Hydrodynamics: I_L(1600 rpm) = {i_lev * 1e6:.2f} uA, "
    f"I_KL = {i_kl * 1e6:.2f} uA, RRDE N = {n_coll:.3f}"
)

# 3. Interfacial Kinetics
e_eq = kinetics.nernst(E0=0.0, n=n, c_ox=1.0, c_red=0.1, T=T)
i_bv = kinetics.butler_volmer(eta=-0.1, i0=1.0e-5, alpha=0.5, n=n, T=T)
b_tafel = kinetics.tafel_slope(alpha=0.5, n=n, T=T)
print(
    f"Kinetics: E_eq = {e_eq:.4f} V, I_BV(-0.1 V) = {i_bv * 1e6:.2f} uA, "
    f"Tafel slope = {b_tafel * 1e3:.1f} mV/dec"
)

# 4. Voltammetry
i_rs = voltammetry.randles_sevcik(v=0.1, c_bulk=c_bulk, D=D, area=area, n=n, T=T)
nich = voltammetry.nicholson_psi(delta_ep=0.085, v=0.1, D=D, n=n, T=T, in_volts=True)
ma = voltammetry.matsuda_ayabe(k0=nich.k0, v=0.1, D=D, n=n, alpha=0.5, T=T)
print(
    f"Voltammetry: I_p = {i_rs * 1e6:.2f} uA, "
    f"Nicholson k0 = {nich.k0:.2e} m/s ({ma.classification})"
)

# 5. Microelectrodes (UME)
a_ume = 12.5e-6  # 25 um diameter disk
i_ss = microelectrodes.microdisc_limiting_current(radius=a_ume, n=n, D=D, c_bulk=c_bulk)
i_tr = microelectrodes.microdisc_transient(
    t=0.01, radius=a_ume, n=n, D=D, c_bulk=c_bulk
)
print(
    f"Microelectrodes: I_ss = {i_ss * 1e9:.2f} nA, "
    f"I_transient(10 ms) = {i_tr * 1e9:.2f} nA"
)

# 6. SECM Approach Curves
L = np.array([0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0])
it_pos = secm.secm_approach_positive_feedback(L, RG=5.0)
it_neg = secm.secm_approach_negative_feedback(L, RG=5.0)
it_kin = secm.secm_approach_curve(L, RG=5.0, kappa=2.0)
print(
    f"SECM (L=0.5): I_T(+) = {it_pos[1]:.3f}, "
    f"I_T(kappa=2) = {it_kin[1]:.3f}, I_T(-) = {it_neg[1]:.3f}"
)

docs.title: Diagnostics & Post-Processing
docs.text: The softpotato.techniques post-processing suite operates directly on TechniqueResult (and RDESweepResult) objects returned by simulate(), simulate_sweep(), and simulate_rde_sweep(), extracting peak metrics, diffusion coefficients, and heterogeneous rate constants without custom boilerplate.

docs.title: Available Diagnostic Functions
docs.text:
Function Input Extracted Quantities Return Type find_peaks CV / LSV / SWV / DPV TechniqueResult \(E_{pa}\), \(I_{pa}\), \(E_{pc}\), \(I_{pc}\), \(E_{p/2}\), \(\Delta E_p\), \(E_{1/2}\), \(\|I_{pa}/I_{pc}\|\) CVDiagnostics (or list[PeakInfo] with return_all=True) analyze_randles_sevcik Sequence/mapping of CV/LSV TechniqueResult Diffusion coefficient \(D\), slope, intercept, \(R^2\) RandlesSevcikFitResult analyze_nicholson Quasi-reversible CV TechniqueResult \(\Delta E_p\), Nicholson \(\Psi\), \(k^0\), Matsuda–Ayabe \(\Lambda\) & regime NicholsonDiagnostics analyze_cottrell Chronoamperometry TechniqueResult Diffusion coefficient \(D\), background \(I_{\text{bg}}\), \(R^2\) CottrellFitResult analyze_levich RDESweepResult or RDE TechniqueResult list Diffusion coefficient \(D\), Levich constant \(B\), \(R^2\) LevichFitResult analyze_koutecky_levich RDESweepResult at mixed-control potential Kinetic current \(I_K\), \(k(E)\), Levich \(B\), \(D\), \(R^2\) KouteckyLevichFitResult analyze_sand Chronopotentiometry TechniqueResult Transition time \(\tau\), theoretical \(\tau\), Sand product \(\|I\|\sqrt{\tau}\), \(D\) SandDiagnostics analyze_tafel Voltammetric TechniqueResult + E0 Tafel slope \(b\) (V/dec & mV/dec), \(\alpha\), \(I_0\), optional \(k^0\), \(R^2\) TafelFitResult

Raw Arrays Supported Too

Every diagnostic function also accepts raw NumPy arrays (for example find_peaks(E, I) or analyze_cottrell(t, I, ...)), so you can apply the exact same analysis pipeline to experimental potentiostat exports.

docs.title: Full Runnable Script
docs.text:
"""User Guide: Post-Processing & Electrochemical Diagnostics.

Demonstrates all diagnostic functions in softpotato.techniques on TechniqueResult objects:
1. find_peaks() — anodic/cathodic peak detection, parabolic refinement, delta_Ep, E_half
2. analyze_randles_sevcik() — multi-scan-rate D extraction
3. analyze_nicholson() — k0 extraction and Matsuda-Ayabe regime classification
4. analyze_cottrell() — chronoamperometric D extraction
5. analyze_levich() — RDE mass-transport D extraction
6. analyze_koutecky_levich() — RDE mixed kinetic/mass-transport I_K and D extraction
7. analyze_sand() — chronopotentiometric transition time tau and D extraction
8. analyze_tafel() — Tafel slope, alpha, exchange current I0, and k0 extraction
"""

from softpotato.geometry import PlanarGeometry
from softpotato.reactions import ButlerVolmer, NernstianEquilibrium, Species
from softpotato.techniques import (
    Chronoamperometry,
    Chronopotentiometry,
    CyclicVoltammetry,
    LinearSweepVoltammetry,
    analyze_cottrell,
    analyze_koutecky_levich,
    analyze_levich,
    analyze_nicholson,
    analyze_randles_sevcik,
    analyze_sand,
    analyze_tafel,
    find_peaks,
    simulate,
    simulate_rde_sweep,
    simulate_sweep,
)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. Physical System (SI units: m^2/s, mol/m^3 = mM, m^2, m/s)
# ==============================================================================
E0 = 0.0
D = 1.0e-9
c_bulk = 1.0
area = 7.07e-6
geometry = PlanarGeometry(area)

ox = Species("Ox", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=c_bulk, standard_potential=E0)
red = Species("Red", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=0.0)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. Peak Detection (find_peaks) & Nicholson Analysis (analyze_nicholson)
# ==============================================================================
bv_quasi = ButlerVolmer(k0=5.0e-5, alpha=0.5, E0=E0, n=1)
cv = CyclicVoltammetry(
    E_start=0.4, E_vertex1=-0.4, E_vertex2=0.4, scan_rate=0.1, dE=0.002
)
cv_result = simulate(cv, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=bv_quasi)

peaks = find_peaks(cv_result)
all_peaks = find_peaks(cv_result, return_all=True)
print("=== find_peaks() ===")
print(
    f"  Cathodic peak: E_pc = {peaks.cathodic_peak.E_peak:.4f} V, "
    f"I_pc = {peaks.cathodic_peak.I_peak * 1e6:.2f} uA"
)
print(
    f"  Anodic peak:   E_pa = {peaks.anodic_peak.E_peak:.4f} V, "
    f"I_pa = {peaks.anodic_peak.I_peak * 1e6:.2f} uA"
)
print(
    f"  delta_Ep = {peaks.delta_Ep * 1e3:.1f} mV, "
    f"E_half = {peaks.E_half:.4f} V, "
    f"|I_pa/I_pc| = {peaks.peak_current_ratio:.3f} "
    f"(total peaks found: {len(all_peaks)})"
)

nich = analyze_nicholson(cv_result, D=D, n=1)
print("\n=== analyze_nicholson() ===")
print(
    f"  delta_Ep = {nich.delta_Ep_mv:.1f} mV, Psi = {nich.psi:.3f}, "
    f"k0 = {nich.k0:.2e} m/s, Lambda = {nich.lambda_param:.2f}, regime = {nich.regime!r}"
)

# ==============================================================================
# 3. Multi-Scan-Rate Randles-Sevcik Analysis (analyze_randles_sevcik)
# ==============================================================================
nernst = NernstianEquilibrium(E0=E0, n=1)
scan_rates = [0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5]
cv_sweep = simulate_sweep(
    lambda v: CyclicVoltammetry(
        E_start=0.4, E_vertex1=-0.4, E_vertex2=0.4, scan_rate=v, dE=0.004
    ),
    [ox, red],
    values=scan_rates,
    geometry=geometry,
    kinetics=nernst,
)
rs_fit = analyze_randles_sevcik(cv_sweep, n=1, area=area, c_bulk=c_bulk)
print("\n=== analyze_randles_sevcik() ===")
print(f"  D = {rs_fit.d:.3e} m^2/s (true: {D:.3e}), R^2 = {rs_fit.r_squared:.5f}")

# ==============================================================================
# 4. Cottrell Chronoamperometry Analysis (analyze_cottrell)
# ==============================================================================
ca = Chronoamperometry(E_step=-0.4, duration=2.0)
ca_result = simulate(ca, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=nernst)
cott_fit = analyze_cottrell(ca_result, n=1, area=area, c_bulk=c_bulk, t_min=0.05)
print("\n=== analyze_cottrell() ===")
print(f"  D = {cott_fit.d:.3e} m^2/s (true: {D:.3e}), R^2 = {cott_fit.r_squared:.5f}")

# ==============================================================================
# 5. Levich & Koutecky-Levich RDE Analysis
# ==============================================================================
rpms = [400.0, 900.0, 1600.0, 2500.0]
rde_rev = simulate_rde_sweep(
    rpms=rpms,
    E_start=0.3,
    E_end=-0.4,
    scan_rate=0.05,
    D=D,
    c_bulk=c_bulk,
    area=area,
    kinetics=nernst,
    dE=0.005,
)
levich_fit = analyze_levich(rde_rev, n=1, area=area, c_bulk=c_bulk)
print("\n=== analyze_levich() ===")
print(
    f"  D = {levich_fit.d:.3e} m^2/s (true: {D:.3e}), "
    f"B = {levich_fit.levich_constant:.3e}, R^2 = {levich_fit.r_squared:.5f}"
)

rde_kin = simulate_rde_sweep(
    rpms=rpms,
    E_start=0.3,
    E_end=-0.4,
    scan_rate=0.05,
    D=D,
    c_bulk=c_bulk,
    area=area,
    kinetics=bv_quasi,
    dE=0.005,
)
kl_fit = analyze_koutecky_levich(
    rde_kin, potential=-0.15, n=1, area=area, c_bulk=c_bulk
)
print("\n=== analyze_koutecky_levich() ===")
print(
    f"  I_K = {kl_fit.i_k * 1e6:.2f} uA, k_rate = {kl_fit.k_rate:.2e} m/s, "
    f"D = {kl_fit.d:.3e} m^2/s, R^2 = {kl_fit.r_squared:.5f}"
)

# ==============================================================================
# 6. Sand Chronopotentiometry Analysis (analyze_sand)
# ==============================================================================
cp = Chronopotentiometry(current=-1.5e-5, duration=4.0)
cp_result = simulate(cp, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=bv_quasi)
sand_diag = analyze_sand(cp_result, n=1, area=area, c_bulk=c_bulk, D=D)
print("\n=== analyze_sand() ===")
print(
    f"  tau = {sand_diag.tau:.4f} s (theoretical: {sand_diag.tau_theoretical:.4f} s), "
    f"D_est = {sand_diag.D_estimated:.3e} m^2/s, method = {sand_diag.detection_method!r}"
)

# ==============================================================================
# 7. Tafel Kinetic Analysis (analyze_tafel)
# ==============================================================================
bv_slow = ButlerVolmer(k0=1.0e-6, alpha=0.5, E0=E0, n=1)
lsv = LinearSweepVoltammetry(E_start=0.0, E_end=-0.35, scan_rate=0.05, dE=0.002)
lsv_result = simulate(lsv, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=bv_slow)
tafel_fit = analyze_tafel(
    lsv_result,
    E0=E0,
    overpotential_window=(-0.18, -0.07),
    branch="cathodic",
    n=1,
    area=area,
    c_bulk=c_bulk,
)
print("\n=== analyze_tafel() ===")
print(
    f"  Tafel slope = {tafel_fit.slope_mv:.1f} mV/dec, alpha = {tafel_fit.alpha:.3f}, "
    f"I0 = {tafel_fit.i0:.2e} A, k0 = {tafel_fit.k0:.2e} m/s, "
    f"R^2 = {tafel_fit.r_squared:.5f}"
)

docs.title: Plotting Suite
docs.text: softpotato.techniques includes a declarative Matplotlib plotting suite. Every renderer accepts an optional ax parameter to draw onto existing axes and returns (fig, ax) (or (fig, axes) for plot_summary()) without calling plt.show().

docs.title: Core & Technique-Specific Renderers
docs.text: Function Target Key Options plot_result Any TechniqueResult Dispatches via result.default_plot or kind ('voltammogram', 'i_vs_t', 'E_vs_t', 'c_vs_x', 'Q_vs_t', 'dpv', 'swv', 'scv'). plot_voltammogram CV, LSV, RDE TechniqueResult cycle (int, 'all', or None), peaks (True, CVDiagnostics, or PeakInfo list). plot_summary Any TechniqueResult Multi-panel summary combining default_plot, i_vs_t, E_vs_t, and c_vs_x. plot_sweep simulate_sweep() or RDESweepResult Overlays multiple traces with automatic labels (labels, legend_title). plot_dpv DifferentialPulseVoltammetry show_components=True overlays \(I_{\text{pulse}}\) and \(I_{\text{pre}}\). plot_swv SquareWaveVoltammetry show_components=True overlays \(I_{\text{forward}}\) and \(I_{\text{reverse}}\). plot_scv SampledCurrentVoltammetry sample_times selects \(\tau\) values for \(I(\tau)\) vs. \(E_{\text{step}}\).

docs.title: Diagnostic Regression Plots
docs.text: Function Paired Diagnostic Plotted Axes plot_peaks find_peaks() \(I\) vs. \(E\) with anodic/cathodic peak markers and \(\Delta E_p\) title. plot_randles_sevcik analyze_randles_sevcik() \(I_p\) vs. \(\sqrt{v}\) scatter + linear/nonlinear regression fit. plot_cottrell analyze_cottrell() \(I\) vs. \(t^{-1/2}\) scatter + regression fit. plot_levich analyze_levich() \(I_L\) vs. \(\omega^{1/2}\) scatter + regression fit. plot_koutecky_levich analyze_koutecky_levich() \(\|I\|^{-1}\) vs. \(\omega^{-1/2}\) scatter + regression fit. plot_tafel analyze_tafel() \(\eta\) vs. \(\log_{10}\|I\|\) scatter + Tafel line fit.

docs.title: Full Runnable Script
docs.text:
"""User Guide: Declarative & Diagnostic Plotting Suite.

Demonstrates all plotting functions in softpotato.techniques on TechniqueResult objects:
1. plot_result() — technique-aware default and explicit kind dispatch
2. plot_voltammogram() — voltammograms with multi-cycle and peak overlay options
3. plot_peaks() — annotated anodic/cathodic peak diagnostics
4. plot_summary() — multi-panel summary figure
5. plot_sweep() — overlaying CV and RDE parameter sweeps
6. plot_randles_sevcik(), plot_tafel(), plot_levich(), plot_koutecky_levich()
7. plot_dpv(), plot_swv(), plot_scv() — pulse and sampled-current voltammograms
"""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from softpotato.geometry import PlanarGeometry
from softpotato.reactions import ButlerVolmer, NernstianEquilibrium, Species
from softpotato.techniques import (
    CyclicVoltammetry,
    DifferentialPulseVoltammetry,
    LinearSweepVoltammetry,
    SampledCurrentVoltammetry,
    SquareWaveVoltammetry,
    analyze_koutecky_levich,
    analyze_levich,
    analyze_randles_sevcik,
    analyze_tafel,
    plot_dpv,
    plot_koutecky_levich,
    plot_levich,
    plot_peaks,
    plot_randles_sevcik,
    plot_result,
    plot_scv,
    plot_summary,
    plot_sweep,
    plot_swv,
    plot_tafel,
    plot_voltammogram,
    simulate,
    simulate_rde_sweep,
    simulate_sweep,
)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. Physical System (SI units)
# ==============================================================================
E0 = 0.0
D = 1.0e-9
c_bulk = 1.0
area = 7.07e-6
geometry = PlanarGeometry(area)

ox = Species("Ox", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=c_bulk, standard_potential=E0)
red = Species("Red", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=0.0)
nernst = NernstianEquilibrium(E0=E0, n=1)
bv_quasi = ButlerVolmer(k0=5.0e-5, alpha=0.5, E0=E0, n=1)
bv_slow = ButlerVolmer(k0=1.0e-6, alpha=0.5, E0=E0, n=1)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. Core Single-Result & Summary Plots
# ==============================================================================
cv = CyclicVoltammetry(
    E_start=0.4, E_vertex1=-0.4, E_vertex2=0.4, scan_rate=0.1, n_cycles=2, dE=0.004
)
cv_result = simulate(cv, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=bv_quasi)

fig1, ax1 = plot_result(cv_result)
ax1.set_title("plot_result() Default (CV)")

fig2, ax2 = plot_voltammogram(cv_result, cycle="all")
ax2.set_title("plot_voltammogram(cycle='all')")

fig3, ax3 = plot_peaks(cv_result)
fig_sum, axes_sum = plot_summary(cv_result)

# ==============================================================================
# 3. Parameter Sweeps & Diagnostic Regression Plots
# ==============================================================================
scan_rates = [0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2]
cv_sweep = simulate_sweep(
    lambda v: CyclicVoltammetry(
        E_start=0.4, E_vertex1=-0.4, E_vertex2=0.4, scan_rate=v, dE=0.005
    ),
    [ox, red],
    values=scan_rates,
    geometry=geometry,
    kinetics=nernst,
)
rs_fit = analyze_randles_sevcik(cv_sweep, n=1, area=area, c_bulk=c_bulk)

fig_swp, ax_swp = plot_sweep(cv_sweep, legend_title="Scan Rate")
fig_rs, ax_rs = plot_randles_sevcik(cv_sweep, rs_fit)

# Tafel plot on LSV
lsv = LinearSweepVoltammetry(E_start=0.0, E_end=-0.35, scan_rate=0.05, dE=0.002)
lsv_result = simulate(lsv, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=bv_slow)
tafel_fit = analyze_tafel(
    lsv_result,
    E0=E0,
    overpotential_window=(-0.18, -0.07),
    branch="cathodic",
    n=1,
    area=area,
    c_bulk=c_bulk,
)
fig_taf, ax_taf = plot_tafel(
    lsv_result,
    tafel_fit,
    E0=E0,
    overpotential_window=(-0.18, -0.07),
    branch="cathodic",
)

# Levich & Koutecky-Levich plots on RDE sweeps
rpms = [400.0, 900.0, 1600.0, 2500.0]
rde_sweep = simulate_rde_sweep(
    rpms=rpms,
    E_start=0.3,
    E_end=-0.4,
    scan_rate=0.05,
    D=D,
    c_bulk=c_bulk,
    area=area,
    kinetics=bv_quasi,
    dE=0.005,
)
lev_fit = analyze_levich(rde_sweep, n=1, area=area, c_bulk=c_bulk)
kl_fit = analyze_koutecky_levich(
    rde_sweep, potential=-0.15, n=1, area=area, c_bulk=c_bulk
)

fig_lev, ax_lev = plot_levich(rde_sweep, lev_fit)
fig_kl, ax_kl = plot_koutecky_levich(rde_sweep, kl_fit, potential=-0.15)

# ==============================================================================
# 4. Pulse & Sampled-Current Voltammetry Plots
# ==============================================================================
dpv = DifferentialPulseVoltammetry(
    E_start=0.3,
    E_end=-0.3,
    step_height=0.01,
    pulse_amplitude=-0.05,
    pulse_width=0.05,
    pulse_period=0.2,
)
dpv_result = simulate(dpv, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=nernst)
fig_dpv, ax_dpv = plot_dpv(dpv_result, show_components=True)

swv = SquareWaveVoltammetry(
    E_start=0.3, E_end=-0.3, step_height=0.01, amplitude=0.025, frequency=15.0
)
swv_result = simulate(swv, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=nernst)
fig_swv, ax_swv = plot_swv(swv_result, show_components=True)

scv = SampledCurrentVoltammetry(
    E_start=0.3,
    E_end=-0.3,
    dE=0.05,
    duration=1.0,
    sample_times=[0.2, 0.5, 1.0],
)
scv_result = simulate(scv, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=nernst)
fig_scv, ax_scv = plot_scv(scv_result)

plt.show()

docs.title: Pulse & Sampled-Current Voltammetry
docs.text: Pulse and sampled-current techniques sample Faradaic current at specific windows after potential steps to enhance sensitivity and discriminate against capacitive background currents.

docs.title: SampledCurrentVoltammetry (SCV)
docs.text:
Simulates a family of independent constant-potential steps across a potential window and samples \(I(\tau)\) at fixed sampling time(s) \(\tau \in (0, t_{\max}]\).

Parameter Type Units Description potentials Sequence[float], optional \(\text{V}\) Explicit list/array of step potentials (mutually exclusive with E_start/E_end/dE). E_start, E_end, dE float, optional \(\text{V}\) Potential window bounds and positive step increment (step_height is an alias for dE). duration float \(\text{s}\) Constant-potential hold duration (\(> 0\)) shared by all steps. sample_times float or Sequence[float], optional \(\text{s}\) Sampling time(s) \(\tau \in (0, t_{\max}]\) used by result.sample_currents(). E_quiet, t_quiet optional \(\text{V}\), \(\text{s}\) Optional resting hold applied before every step.

docs.title: DifferentialPulseVoltammetry (DPV)
docs.text:
Superimposes potential pulses of amplitude \(\Delta E_p\) and width \(t_p\) onto a staircase ramp with period \(\tau\) and step height \(\Delta E_s\).

Parameter Type Units Description E_start, E_end float \(\text{V}\) Initial and final staircase base potentials. step_height float \(\text{V}\) Staircase step magnitude \(\Delta E_s > 0\). pulse_amplitude float \(\text{V}\) Pulse amplitude \(\Delta E_p \neq 0\) (negative for cathodic pulses, positive for anodic). pulse_width float \(\text{s}\) Pulse duration \(t_p > 0\). pulse_period float \(\text{s}\) Total cycle period \(\tau > t_p\). sample_fraction float, default 0.1 — Fraction \(\in (0, 1]\) at the end of each base/pulse segment averaged by sample_currents().

docs.title: SquareWaveVoltammetry (SWV)
docs.text:
Superimposes a symmetric square wave of amplitude \(E_{\text{sw}} > 0\) and frequency \(f > 0\) (period \(\tau = 1/f\), half-period \(t_p = 1/(2f)\)) onto a staircase ramp.

Parameter Type Units Description E_start, E_end float \(\text{V}\) Initial and final staircase potentials. step_height float \(\text{V}\) Staircase step magnitude \(\Delta E_s > 0\). amplitude float \(\text{V}\) Square-wave amplitude \(E_{\text{sw}} > 0\). frequency float \(\text{Hz}\) Square-wave frequency \(f > 0\). sample_fraction float, default 0.1 — Fraction \(\in (0, 1]\) at the end of each half-cycle averaged by sample_currents().

docs.title: Full Runnable Script
docs.text:
"""User Guide: Pulse & Sampled-Current Voltammetry (SCV, DPV, SWV).

Demonstrates:
1. SampledCurrentVoltammetry (SCV) across a potential window
2. DifferentialPulseVoltammetry (DPV)
3. SquareWaveVoltammetry (SWV)
"""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from softpotato.geometry import PlanarGeometry
from softpotato.reactions import ButlerVolmer, Species
from softpotato.techniques import (
    DifferentialPulseVoltammetry,
    SampledCurrentVoltammetry,
    SquareWaveVoltammetry,
    plot_result,
    simulate,
)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. Physical System (SI units: m^2/s, mol/m^3 = mM, m^2, m/s)
# ==============================================================================
E0 = 0.0  # Formal potential [V]
D = 1.0e-9  # Diffusion coefficient [m^2/s]
c_bulk = 1.0  # Bulk concentration of Ox [mol/m^3] (= 1.0 mM)
k0 = 1.0e-3  # Heterogeneous rate constant [m/s]
alpha = 0.5  # Transfer coefficient [-]
area = 7.07e-6  # Electrode area [m^2]

ox = Species(
    "Ox", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=c_bulk, standard_potential=E0, n_electrons=1
)
red = Species("Red", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=0.0)
kinetics = ButlerVolmer(k0=k0, alpha=alpha, E0=E0, n=1)
geometry = PlanarGeometry(area)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. Sampled-Current Voltammetry (SCV)
# ==============================================================================
scv = SampledCurrentVoltammetry(
    E_start=0.3,
    E_end=-0.3,
    dE=0.05,
    duration=2.0,
    sample_times=[0.5, 1.0, 2.0],
)
res_scv = simulate(scv, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=kinetics)
sampled = res_scv.sample_currents()
print(f"SCV: {scv.n_steps} steps, sampled at tau = {scv.sample_times} s")

fig_scv, ax_scv = plot_result(res_scv)
ax_scv.set_title("Sampled-Current Voltammetry (SCV)")

# ==============================================================================
# 3. Differential Pulse Voltammetry (DPV)
# ==============================================================================
dpv = DifferentialPulseVoltammetry(
    E_start=0.3,
    E_end=-0.3,
    step_height=0.02,
    pulse_amplitude=-0.025,
    pulse_width=0.05,
    pulse_period=0.5,
)
res_dpv = simulate(dpv, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=kinetics)
E_base, _, _, i_diff_dpv = dpv.sample_currents(res_dpv.time, res_dpv.current)
print(
    f"DPV: {dpv.n_steps} pulses, peak |dI| = {abs(i_diff_dpv).max() * 1e6:.2f} uA "
    f"at E = {E_base[abs(i_diff_dpv).argmax()]:.3f} V"
)

fig_dpv, ax_dpv = plot_result(res_dpv)
ax_dpv.set_title("Differential Pulse Voltammetry (DPV)")

# ==============================================================================
# 4. Square-Wave Voltammetry (SWV)
# ==============================================================================
swv = SquareWaveVoltammetry(
    E_start=0.3,
    E_end=-0.3,
    step_height=0.02,
    amplitude=0.025,
    frequency=10.0,
)
res_swv = simulate(swv, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=kinetics)
E_step, _, _, i_net_swv = swv.sample_currents(res_swv.time, res_swv.current)
print(
    f"SWV: {swv.n_steps} cycles (f = {swv.frequency} Hz), "
    f"peak |dI| = {abs(i_net_swv).max() * 1e6:.2f} uA "
    f"at E = {E_step[abs(i_net_swv).argmax()]:.3f} V"
)

fig_swv, ax_swv = plot_result(res_swv)
ax_swv.set_title("Square-Wave Voltammetry (SWV)")

plt.show()

docs.title: Rotating Disk Electrode (RDE)
docs.text: RotatingDiskElectrode couples any potentiostatic waveform (defaulting to LinearSweepVoltammetry) with forced hydrodynamic convection at a rotating disk electrode.

docs.title: Hydrodynamic Models
docs.text:
Two mass-transport models are supported via the model parameter:

  • "nernst_layer" (default): Nernst stagnant diffusion layer approximation on \(x \in [0, \delta_N]\) with a bulk Dirichlet boundary condition at \(x = \delta_N\):

$$ \delta_N = 1.610 \, D^{1/3} \nu^{1/6} \omega^{-1/2} $$

  • "convective_diffusion": Full Levich axial convective-diffusion PDE on \(x \in [0, k \delta_N]\) (default \(k = 3.0\)) including the von Kármán axial fluid velocity toward the disk:

$$ v_x(x) = -0.51023 \, \omega^{3/2} \nu^{-1/2} x^2 $$

docs.title: RotatingDiskElectrode & simulate_rde_sweep
docs.text:
Parameter Type Units Description waveform BaseTechnique, optional — Custom potentiostatic waveform (mutually exclusive with E_start, E_end, scan_rate). E_start, E_end, scan_rate float, optional \(\text{V}\), \(\text{V}/\text{s}\) Direct LSV parameters when waveform is omitted. omega / omegas float / Sequence[float] \(\text{rad}/\text{s}\) Angular rotation velocity (\(> 0\)). Mutually exclusive with rpm / rpms. rpm / rpms float / Sequence[float] \(\text{rpm}\) Rotational speed in revolutions per minute (\(> 0\)). Mutually exclusive with omega / omegas. kinematic_viscosity float, default 1e-6 \(\text{m}^2/\text{s}\) Electrolyte kinematic viscosity \(\nu > 0\) (\(10^{-6}\text{ m}^2/\text{s}\) for water at \(298\text{ K}\)). model 'nernst_layer' or 'convective_diffusion' — Hydrodynamic transport model. domain_factor float, optional — Multiplier \(k > 0\) on \(\delta_N\) for mesh extent (defaults to 1.0 for Nernst layer, 3.0 for convective diffusion).

simulate_rde_sweep() returns an RDESweepResult containing .omegas, .rpms, .limiting_currents, and .results, which can be passed directly to plot_sweep(), analyze_levich(), or analyze_koutecky_levich().

docs.title: Full Runnable Script
docs.text:
"""User Guide: Rotating Disk Electrode (RDE) & Hydrodynamic Sweeps.

Demonstrates:
1. Single-rate RotatingDiskElectrode simulation via simulate()
2. Multi-rotation-rate sweep with simulate_rde_sweep()
3. Comparison of simulated limiting currents against the analytical Levich equation
"""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from softpotato.analytical.hydrodynamics import levich
from softpotato.geometry import PlanarGeometry
from softpotato.reactions import ButlerVolmer, Species
from softpotato.techniques import (
    RotatingDiskElectrode,
    plot_result,
    plot_sweep,
    simulate,
    simulate_rde_sweep,
)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. Physical System (SI units: m^2/s, mol/m^3 = mM, m^2, m/s)
# ==============================================================================
E0 = 0.0  # Formal potential [V]
D = 1.0e-9  # Diffusion coefficient [m^2/s]
c_bulk = 1.0  # Bulk concentration of Ox [mol/m^3] (= 1.0 mM)
nu = 1.0e-6  # Electrolyte kinematic viscosity [m^2/s] (water at 298 K)
k0 = 1.0e-3  # Heterogeneous rate constant [m/s]
alpha = 0.5  # Transfer coefficient [-]
area = 1.96e-5  # Disk electrode area [m^2] (5 mm diameter disk)

ox = Species(
    "Ox", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=c_bulk, standard_potential=E0, n_electrons=1
)
red = Species("Red", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=0.0)
kinetics = ButlerVolmer(k0=k0, alpha=alpha, E0=E0, n=1)
geometry = PlanarGeometry(area)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. Single Rotation Rate RDE via simulate()
# ==============================================================================
rde = RotatingDiskElectrode(
    E_start=0.4,
    E_end=-0.4,
    scan_rate=0.05,
    rpm=1600,
    kinematic_viscosity=nu,
    model="nernst_layer",
)
res_rde = simulate(rde, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=kinetics)
delta_n = rde.diffusion_layer_thickness(D)
print(
    f"RDE (1600 rpm): omega = {rde.omega:.2f} rad/s, "
    f"delta_N = {delta_n * 1e6:.2f} um, "
    f"I_lim(sim) = {abs(res_rde.current[-1]) * 1e6:.2f} uA"
)

fig_rde, ax_rde = plot_result(res_rde)
ax_rde.set_title("RDE Linear Sweep Voltammogram (1600 rpm)")

# ==============================================================================
# 3. Multi-Rotation-Rate Sweep with simulate_rde_sweep() & Butler-Volmer
# ==============================================================================
rpms = [400, 900, 1600, 2500]
sweep_res = simulate_rde_sweep(
    E_start=0.4,
    E_end=-0.4,
    scan_rate=0.05,
    rpms=rpms,
    kinematic_viscosity=nu,
    model="convective_diffusion",
    D=D,
    c_bulk=c_bulk,
    kinetics=kinetics,
    area=area,
    solver_kwargs={"rtol": 1e-6, "atol": 1e-9},
)

for rpm, omega, i_lim_sim in zip(rpms, sweep_res.omegas, sweep_res.limiting_currents):
    i_lim_levich = levich(omega=omega, n=1, D=D, c_bulk=c_bulk, area=area, nu=nu)
    print(
        f"  {rpm:>4d} rpm: |I_lim(sim)| = {abs(i_lim_sim) * 1e6:>7.2f} uA, "
        f"Levich = {i_lim_levich * 1e6:>7.2f} uA"
    )

fig_sweep, ax_sweep = plot_sweep(sweep_res, legend_title="Rotation Rate")
ax_sweep.set_title("RDE Rotation-Rate Series (Convective-Diffusion, Butler-Volmer)")

plt.show()

docs.title: Step Techniques (CA & CP)
docs.text: Step techniques apply abrupt jumps in either electrode potential (Chronoamperometry, potentiostatic) or applied current (Chronopotentiometry, galvanostatic).

docs.title: Chronoamperometry (Potentiostatic)
docs.text:
Supports three construction modes, each optionally preceded by a resting quiet hold (E_quiet, t_quiet):

  1. Single-step: Chronoamperometry(E_step=..., duration=...)
  2. Double-step: Chronoamperometry(E_step1=..., E_step2=..., t_step1=..., t_step2=...)
  3. Multi-step: Chronoamperometry(potentials=[...], durations=[...])
Parameter Type Units Description E_step / E_step1, E_step2 / potentials float / Sequence[float] \(\text{V}\) Applied step potential(s). duration / t_step1, t_step2 / durations float / Sequence[float] \(\text{s}\) Step duration(s) (\(> 0\)). E_quiet float, optional \(\text{V}\) Initial resting potential applied before the first step. t_quiet float, default 0.0 \(\text{s}\) Resting duration (\(\ge 0\)). Requires E_quiet when \(> 0\).

docs.title: Chronopotentiometry (Galvanostatic)
docs.text:
Supports single-step (current, duration) and multi-step / current-reversal (currents, durations) modes, with optional (I_quiet, t_quiet).

Under IUPAC polarity, negative current (\(I < 0\)) is cathodic (reduction) and positive current (\(I > 0\)) is anodic (oxidation).

Parameter Type Units Description current / currents float / Sequence[float] \(\text{A}\) Applied Faradaic current(s). duration / durations float / Sequence[float] \(\text{s}\) Step duration(s) (\(> 0\)). I_quiet float, optional \(\text{A}\) Initial resting current applied before the first step. t_quiet float, default 0.0 \(\text{s}\) Resting duration (\(\ge 0\)). Requires I_quiet when \(> 0\).

Automatic Sand Transition Time (\(\tau\))

When simulating Chronopotentiometry via simulate(), Soft Potato automatically detects the Sand transition time \(\tau\) (when surface reactant concentration depletes to zero) and stores it in result.metadata["transition_time"].

docs.text:
"""User Guide: Step Techniques — Chronoamperometry (CA) & Chronopotentiometry (CP).

Demonstrates:
1. Single-step and double-step Chronoamperometry (potentiostatic)
2. Single-step and current-reversal Chronopotentiometry (galvanostatic)
3. Automatic Sand transition time detection in CP metadata
"""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from softpotato.geometry import PlanarGeometry
from softpotato.reactions import ButlerVolmer, Species
from softpotato.techniques import (
    Chronoamperometry,
    Chronopotentiometry,
    plot_result,
    simulate,
)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. Physical System (SI units: m^2/s, mol/m^3 = mM, m^2, m/s)
# ==============================================================================
E0 = 0.0  # Formal potential [V]
D = 1.0e-9  # Diffusion coefficient [m^2/s]
c_bulk = 1.0  # Bulk concentration of Ox [mol/m^3] (= 1.0 mM)
k0 = 1.0e-3  # Heterogeneous rate constant [m/s]
alpha = 0.5  # Transfer coefficient [-]
area = 7.07e-6  # Electrode area [m^2]

ox = Species(
    "Ox", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=c_bulk, standard_potential=E0, n_electrons=1
)
red = Species("Red", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=0.0)
kinetics = ButlerVolmer(k0=k0, alpha=alpha, E0=E0, n=1)
geometry = PlanarGeometry(area)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. Single-Step & Double-Step Chronoamperometry (CA)
# ==============================================================================
ca_single = Chronoamperometry(E_step=-0.4, duration=5.0)
res_ca = simulate(ca_single, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=kinetics)
print(
    f"Single-step CA: i(0.5 s) = {res_ca.current[len(res_ca.time) // 10] * 1e6:.2f} uA, "
    f"i(5.0 s) = {res_ca.current[-1] * 1e6:.2f} uA"
)

# Double-step CA with an initial 0.5 s quiet hold at +0.3 V
ca_double = Chronoamperometry(
    E_step1=-0.4,
    E_step2=0.4,
    t_step1=2.0,
    t_step2=2.0,
    E_quiet=0.3,
    t_quiet=0.5,
)
res_dca = simulate(ca_double, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=kinetics)
print(f"Double-step CA: step transitions at t = {ca_double.event_times} s")

fig_ca, ax_ca = plot_result(res_dca)
ax_ca.set_title("Double-Step Chronoamperometry (with Quiet Hold)")

# ==============================================================================
# 3. Single-Step & Current-Reversal Chronopotentiometry (CP)
# ==============================================================================
# Negative current = cathodic (reduction) under IUPAC convention
cp_single = Chronopotentiometry(current=-1.5e-5, duration=4.0)
res_cp = simulate(cp_single, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=kinetics)
tau = res_cp.metadata.get("transition_time")
print(
    f"Single-step CP: Sand transition time tau = {tau:.3f} s"
    if tau
    else "No transition"
)

fig_cp, ax_cp = plot_result(res_cp)
ax_cp.set_title("Constant-Current Chronopotentiometry")

# Current-reversal CP: reduce for 1.5 s, then oxidize for 1.5 s
cp_rev = Chronopotentiometry(currents=[-1.5e-5, 1.5e-5], durations=[1.5, 1.5])
res_rcp = simulate(cp_rev, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=kinetics)
print(f"Current-reversal CP: reversal at t = {cp_rev.event_times} s")

fig_rcp, ax_rcp = plot_result(res_rcp)
ax_rcp.set_title("Current-Reversal Chronopotentiometry")

plt.show()

docs.title: Voltammetry (LSV & CV)
docs.text: Linear Sweep Voltammetry (LinearSweepVoltammetry) and Cyclic Voltammetry (CyclicVoltammetry) apply a linear potential ramp \(E(t)\) at a constant scan rate \(v = |dE/dt|\). Soft Potato automatically splits cyclic waveforms at their switching vertices (event_times) so the ODE/PDE solver integrates cleanly across slope discontinuities.

docs.title: LinearSweepVoltammetry
docs.text: Parameter Type Units Description E_start float \(\text{V}\) Initial electrode potential. E_end float \(\text{V}\) Final electrode potential (must differ from E_start). scan_rate float \(\text{V}/\text{s}\) Positive scan rate magnitude \(v > 0\). dE float, optional \(\text{V}\) Potential step resolution for the evaluation grid (mutually exclusive with n_points). n_points int, optional — Number of evaluation time points \(\ge 2\) (mutually exclusive with dE).

docs.title: CyclicVoltammetry
docs.text: Parameter Type Units Description E_start float \(\text{V}\) Initial electrode potential. E_vertex1 float \(\text{V}\) First switching vertex potential \(E_{\lambda 1}\) (must differ from E_start). E_vertex2 float \(\text{V}\) Second switching vertex potential \(E_{\lambda 2}\) (must differ from E_vertex1). Set equal to E_start for a standard two-vertex triangular wave. scan_rate float \(\text{V}/\text{s}\) Positive scan rate magnitude \(v > 0\). E_end float, optional \(\text{V}\) Final potential at the end of the last cycle (defaults to E_start). n_cycles int, default 1 — Number of complete voltammetric cycles (\(\ge 1\)). dE / n_points optional \(\text{V}\) / — Evaluation grid resolution (mutually exclusive).

docs.title: Multi-Scan-Rate Sweeps (simulate_sweep)
docs.text: Pass a factory callable lambda v: CyclicVoltammetry(..., scan_rate=v) and values=[...] to simulate_sweep(). Each scan rate automatically constructs a physics-informed diffusion mesh sized to its own experiment duration \(\sqrt{D t_{\max}}\).

docs.text:
"""User Guide: Linear Sweep (LSV) and Cyclic Voltammetry (CV).

Demonstrates:
1. LinearSweepVoltammetry with simulate() and plot_result()
2. Multi-cycle CyclicVoltammetry with Butler-Volmer kinetics
3. Multi-scan-rate parameter sweep with simulate_sweep() and plot_sweep()
"""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from softpotato.geometry import PlanarGeometry
from softpotato.reactions import ButlerVolmer, Species
from softpotato.techniques import (
    CyclicVoltammetry,
    LinearSweepVoltammetry,
    plot_result,
    plot_sweep,
    simulate,
    simulate_sweep,
)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. Physical System (SI units: m^2/s, mol/m^3 = mM, m^2, m/s)
# ==============================================================================
E0 = 0.0  # Formal potential [V]
D = 1.0e-9  # Diffusion coefficient [m^2/s]
c_bulk = 1.0  # Bulk concentration of Ox [mol/m^3] (= 1.0 mM)
k0 = 1.0e-3  # Heterogeneous rate constant [m/s]
alpha = 0.5  # Transfer coefficient [-]
area = 7.07e-6  # Electrode area [m^2] (3 mm diameter disk)

# Species must be ordered [ox, red] for Ox + e- -> Red
ox = Species(
    "Ox", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=c_bulk, standard_potential=E0, n_electrons=1
)
red = Species("Red", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=0.0)
kinetics = ButlerVolmer(k0=k0, alpha=alpha, E0=E0, n=1)
geometry = PlanarGeometry(area)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. Linear Sweep Voltammetry (LSV)
# ==============================================================================
lsv = LinearSweepVoltammetry(E_start=0.4, E_end=-0.4, scan_rate=0.1, dE=0.002)
lsv_result = simulate(lsv, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=kinetics)
print(
    f"LSV: duration = {lsv.duration:.2f} s, "
    f"peak cathodic current = {lsv_result.current.min() * 1e6:.2f} uA"
)

fig_lsv, ax_lsv = plot_result(lsv_result)
ax_lsv.set_title("Linear Sweep Voltammetry (v = 0.1 V/s)")

# ==============================================================================
# 3. Multi-Cycle Cyclic Voltammetry (CV)
# ==============================================================================
cv = CyclicVoltammetry(
    E_start=0.4,
    E_vertex1=-0.4,
    E_vertex2=0.4,
    scan_rate=0.1,
    n_cycles=2,
    dE=0.002,
)
cv_result = simulate(cv, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=kinetics)
print(
    f"CV (2 cycles): duration = {cv.duration:.2f} s, switching times = {cv.event_times}"
)

fig_cv, ax_cv = plot_result(cv_result)
ax_cv.set_title("Cyclic Voltammetry (2 cycles, v = 0.1 V/s)")

# ==============================================================================
# 4. Multi-Scan-Rate Sweep with simulate_sweep()
# ==============================================================================
scan_rates = [0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5]
sweep_results = simulate_sweep(
    lambda v: CyclicVoltammetry(
        E_start=0.4, E_vertex1=-0.4, E_vertex2=0.4, scan_rate=v, dE=0.004
    ),
    [ox, red],
    values=scan_rates,
    geometry=geometry,
    kinetics=kinetics,
)

for v, res in sweep_results.items():
    print(
        f"  v = {v:>4.2f} V/s -> i_pc = {res.current.min() * 1e6:>7.2f} uA, "
        f"i_pa = {res.current.max() * 1e6:>6.2f} uA"
    )

fig_sweep, ax_sweep = plot_sweep(
    sweep_results,
    labels=[f"{v} V/s" for v in scan_rates],
    legend_title="Scan Rate",
)
ax_sweep.set_title("Scan-Rate Series (Cyclic Voltammetry)")

plt.show()

docs.title: Custom Waveforms & Segments
docs.text:
When an experiment does not fit a standard voltammetry or pulse template—such as conditioning holds followed by AC voltammetry or exponential relaxation—you can compose arbitrary excitation signals using CustomWaveform and WaveformSegment building blocks.

CustomWaveform automatically computes total duration, stitches segment boundaries as event_times for piecewise integration, and supports both "potentiostatic" and "galvanostatic" control modes.

docs.title: Available Segment Primitives
docs.text: Segment Class Mathematical Form (\(\tau \in [0, \Delta t]\)) Key Parameters ConstantSegment \(y(\tau) = y_0\) value, duration LinearRampSegment \(y(\tau) = y_{\text{start}} + \frac{y_{\text{end}} - y_{\text{start}}}{\Delta t}\tau\) start, end, duration (or rate) SinusoidalSegment \(y(\tau) = y_0 + A \sin(2\pi f \tau + \phi)\) offset, amplitude, frequency, duration, phase CallableSegment \(y(\tau) = f(\tau)\) func, duration, event_times (optional)

docs.title: CustomWaveform Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Description segments Sequence[WaveformSegment] Non-empty ordered sequence of segment objects. mode 'potentiostatic' or 'galvanostatic' Control mode ('potentiostatic' applies potential in \(\text{V}\); 'galvanostatic' applies current in \(\text{A}\)). n_points int, optional Default number of evaluation points when time_grid() is called without arguments (default 1001).

docs.text:
"""User Guide: Custom Waveforms & Composable Segments.

Demonstrates:
1. Chaining ConstantSegment, LinearRampSegment, SinusoidalSegment, and CallableSegment
2. Simulating a CustomWaveform with simulate()
3. Multi-panel visualization with plot_summary()
"""

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

from softpotato.geometry import PlanarGeometry
from softpotato.reactions import ButlerVolmer, Species
from softpotato.techniques import (
    CallableSegment,
    ConstantSegment,
    CustomWaveform,
    LinearRampSegment,
    SinusoidalSegment,
    plot_summary,
    simulate,
)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. Physical System (SI units: m^2/s, mol/m^3 = mM, m^2, m/s)
# ==============================================================================
E0 = 0.0  # Formal potential [V]
D = 1.0e-9  # Diffusion coefficient [m^2/s]
c_bulk = 1.0  # Bulk concentration of Ox [mol/m^3] (= 1.0 mM)
k0 = 1.0e-3  # Heterogeneous rate constant [m/s]
alpha = 0.5  # Transfer coefficient [-]
area = 7.07e-6  # Electrode area [m^2]

ox = Species(
    "Ox", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=c_bulk, standard_potential=E0, n_electrons=1
)
red = Species("Red", diffusivity=D, bulk_concentration=0.0)
kinetics = ButlerVolmer(k0=k0, alpha=alpha, E0=E0, n=1)
geometry = PlanarGeometry(area)


# ==============================================================================
# 2. Compose Custom Waveform from Primitive Segments
# ==============================================================================
# Example: Conditioning hold -> Linear ramp -> AC sine wave -> Exponential decay
def exp_relaxation(t_local: np.ndarray | float) -> np.ndarray | float:
    """Relax potential exponentially from -0.2 V back toward +0.2 V."""
    return 0.2 - 0.4 * np.exp(-2.0 * np.asarray(t_local))


waveform = CustomWaveform(
    segments=[
        ConstantSegment(value=0.3, duration=0.5),
        LinearRampSegment(start=0.3, end=-0.2, duration=2.5),
        SinusoidalSegment(offset=-0.2, amplitude=0.05, frequency=2.0, duration=1.5),
        CallableSegment(func=exp_relaxation, duration=1.5),
    ],
    mode="potentiostatic",
)

print(f"CustomWaveform total duration: {waveform.duration:.2f} s")
print(f"Segment boundaries: {waveform.segment_boundaries}")
print(f"Interior event times: {waveform.event_times}")

# ==============================================================================
# 3. Simulate & Summarize
# ==============================================================================
result = simulate(waveform, [ox, red], geometry=geometry, kinetics=kinetics)
print(
    f"Simulated {len(result.time)} points; "
    f"current range: [{result.current.min() * 1e6:.2f}, {result.current.max() * 1e6:.2f}] uA"
)

fig, axes = plot_summary(result)
fig.suptitle("Custom Multi-Segment Waveform Simulation", y=1.02)

plt.show()
